gems.name: Agni Mani
gems.magical_effect: Found as meteoritic glass in deserts; vaporizes in any blast (fireball, bead of force) but negates 1d4 points of blast damage per stone worn or carried.

gems.name: Alabaster
gems.magical_effect: No known magical properties; impervious to moisture short-term, making it a good potion container.

gems.name: Alestone
gems.magical_effect: Deflects solid projectiles; bearer must make a Dexterity check to catch or snatch it; increases effective AC by 1 vs. projectiles from the side the stone is on.
gems.notes: More is not better — only one stone's protection applies regardless of quantity.

gems.name: Alexandrite
gems.magical_effect: Favored focal stone for luck, favor, and protection items (luckstones, lodestones).
gems.notes: Appears greenish in daylight, reddish under magical light.

gems.name: Algae
gems.magical_effect: All beings or items in contact with it make saving throws vs. polymorph or shape-change at +2 bonus — even if the change is willing.

gems.name: Amaratha
gems.magical_effect: Absorbs electricity within 10 ft radius; a 1-inch-diameter sphere absorbs up to 6 points of electrical damage and is then consumed at that volume rate. Excess discharge beyond the stone's capacity still affects targets normally.
gems.notes: Too soft for exposed ring or staff settings; suited to protected locations on personal jewelry or ornamental armor.

gems.name: Amber
gems.magical_effect: Spell component and spell ink ingredient in lightning and electrical enchantments (shocking grasp through chain lightning).
gems.incorrect_belief: Falsely believed to ward off disease and plague.

gems.name: Amethyst
gems.magical_effect: Component in communication spells (magic mouth) and Wisdom-augmenting magics; can be transformed into an ioun stone. Worn whole at mornbright (half-hour centered on 8 a.m.) by a being who wears as many pure amethysts as Wisdom points: grants the magical defense adjustment and spell immunities of Wisdom 23 (without bonus spells).
gems.incorrect_belief: Falsely said to ward off drunkenness and neutralize poison.
gems.notes: Represents safety in seer visions; romance when seen in women's dreams. Nine Secrets material

gems.name: Andar
gems.magical_effect: Powdered, boiled with an amethyst/gold/silver dragon scale, then combined with an oily base: alternative ingredient for a potion of treasure finding.

gems.name: Angélar's Skin
gems.magical_effect: Powdered, mixed with seawater, and followed by polymorph self, water breathing, and a free action variant: induces controlled were-shark transformation (permanent, manageable).
gems.notes: Named for the sorcerer Angélar who underwent the transformation. Pink coral, shallow tropical reefs.

gems.name: Aquamarine
gems.magical_effect: Orgonils ritual (exact process unknown, held as a secret in Telflamm): sacrificing an aquamarine causes another gemstone to become two identical copies.

gems.name: Archon
gems.magical_effect: Glows with a faint greenish radiance when magically invisible objects or creatures come within 20 feet.
gems.notes: Also see Fluorspar (the gem-grade variety).

gems.name: Augelite
gems.magical_effect: Magically inert; in fact lessens spell effects in its vicinity: –1 damage per die for spells within 10 ft; +2 bonus to all saves vs. spells and magical effects within the same area.
gems.notes: Cannot be carved into delicate shapes without splitting.

gems.name: Aventurine
gems.magical_effect: Powdered, penetrates magical disguises; touch shatters most illusion and transformation magics.

gems.name: Azurite
gems.magical_effect: Prevents all heat damage to any being in direct flesh-to-gem contact; reduces most fire/flame damage by half.
gems.notes: Related to malachite but restricted to fire protection only.

gems.name: Banded Agate
gems.magical_effect: Powdered in sleeping drafts: used as a spell ink ingredient and potion base.
gems.incorrect_belief: Powder not actually effective as a sleep aid on its own.
gems.notes: Also used as a calming "soothe stone" by merchants during negotiations.

gems.name: Beljuril
gems.magical_effect: Periodically absorbs ambient heat, light, and vibration within 30 ft and discharges as sparkling cold flash (harmless). Chips mounted at the end of lightning wands add 1d6 damage beyond normal. Powdered, prized in spell ink and item-enchanting baths for all electricity-related magic.
gems.notes: Usually fist-sized; extremely hard to cut. Flash rate varies randomly regardless of size.

gems.name: Black Opal
gems.magical_effect: Powdered, mixed with powdered orl and introduced to open flame in the proper way: explosion dealing 6d8 (within 10 ft), 4d8 (11–20 ft), 2d8 (21–30 ft); save vs. petrification for half. Items within 10 ft must save vs. disintegration; 11–20 ft vs. crushing blow.

gems.name: Black Sapphire
gems.magical_effect: Once cut and polished, prevents temporal stasis, time stop, all chronomancy spells, and time sphere spells from functioning within 30 ft. Such magics cease if the gem is brought within 30 ft; some resume after it leaves, others are ended permanently depending on their nature.
gems.notes: Mostly from the Great Rift; prized by dwarves.

gems.name: Bloodstone
gems.magical_effect: Laid on an open wound: instantly closes it, banishes disease and blood poisoning, stops bleeding (dissolves in doing so). Works once per being per lunar cycle. Alternative component for invisibility, divination, and storm magics.
gems.notes: Combined with a sprig of heliotrope: full alternative for the invisibility spell.

gems.name: Bluestone
gems.magical_effect: Powdered and added to water lit by any magical radiance: acts as either neutralize poison or heals 1d2 damage. Added to any magical healing potion: adds a neutralize poison function plus 1d4 additional healing.

gems.name: Blue Quartz
gems.magical_effect: Used in scrying spells; best gem for gems of seeing; sliced and treated for magical eyes (eyes of the eagle, etc.).

gems.name: Boakhar
gems.magical_effect: Erupts in a 7-foot jet of flame lasting 1 round when a magic missile is cast or passes within 10 ft — consuming the gem and dealing 2d4+2 fire damage.
gems.notes: Found in old Sembian/Calishite furniture inlays. Ignites flammable substances touched, never the item the gem came from.

gems.name: Brandeen
gems.magical_effect: Cure for deafness: powdered and added to sap of any living hardwood, a message spell cast on the mixture (vowel sounds only), kept out of sunlight, and drunk within a day.

gems.name: Carnelian
gems.magical_effect: Component in luck- and protection-against-evil spells and items. All saves and ability checks of wearers aided by +1; once properly enspelled and then sacrificed, allows a failed save, system shock, or resurrection roll to be rerolled at +2/+20% bonus (gem vanishes in a flash).

gems.name: Chalcedony
gems.magical_effect: Used in magical items warding undead or with necromantic powers; preferred when human bone is to be avoided. Powdered, enchanted simply: tasteless antidote to alcohol (added to a drink, prevents drunkenness).
gems.notes: Chalcedony is a broad category including carnelians, chrysoprase, and agates; "chalcedony" used specifically refers to the white/gray/black uncolored variety.

gems.name: Chrysoberyl
gems.magical_effect: Used in protection-from-magic-jar, possession, and incorporation-necromancy enchantments; forged with chips/stones into a weapon with the right enchantments: weapon can strike ethereal and gaseous foes at all times. Dust + juice of specific flower: cures mummy rot and all molds/fungal growths instantly on contact. Certain Netherese message stones. Can be transformed into an ioun stone.
gems.notes: Nine Secrets material

gems.name: Chrysocolla
gems.magical_effect: Neutralizes alcohol on contact; ingredient in animate dead spell inks and castings (often thrown as powder into a fire).

gems.name: Chrysoprase
gems.magical_effect: Used in items and inks for invisibility magic and for seeing invisible beings and objects. Can be transformed into an ioun stone.
gems.notes: Nine Secrets material

gems.name: Citrine
gems.magical_effect: Prevents magic jar attacks from affecting any being wearing or carrying one; conversely, whole citrines are a favored gemstone for use as the jar itself.

gems.name: Clelophane
gems.magical_effect: Echo effect: 70% chance to record a silent 3D mental image of the bearer and their surroundings when a spell is cast by or on them. 70% chance to overwrite prior echoes; otherwise adds a new image. Echoes can be called up repeatedly at will; appear as a slightly luminous 10-ft globe beside the stone for 3 rounds.
gems.notes: Images persist indefinitely, always at perfect clarity even if the original scene was confused.

gems.name: Coral
gems.magical_effect: Powdered: highly effective ingredient in potions of healing and extra-healing — reroll all 1s and 2s on hit dice restored.
gems.notes: Pink and crimson varieties used as gemstones.

gems.name: Corstal
gems.magical_effect: When touched by magical radiance of any kind (fireball to faerie fire), mirrors that light's hue and intensity within itself, becoming a light source for 2d12 rounds before fading.

gems.name: Crown of Silver
gems.magical_effect: Powdered and applied to ferrous metals: prevents rusting. Ingredient in spell ink and component of the everbright spell. Can substitute for iron filings in most castings (such as protection from evil).
gems.notes: Black metallic bands within the stone.

gems.name: Datchas
gems.magical_effect: If powdered datchas is ingested by a wizard (with a nonalcoholic drink), it doubles the duration of a spider climb spell affecting them.

gems.name: Diamond
gems.magical_effect: Near-universal spell ink ingredient (especially vision, divination, and locating-object spells). Best gems for gems of seeing. Essential in a helm of brilliance. Worn at throat or head: wards off dream visions and enchantment/charm magics; +2 bonus to all saves vs. enchantment/charm. Diamond dust used in neutralize poison processes. Best used at highsun (noon).
gems.notes: Powdered diamond used at noon: increases magical working efficacy by 2 or 25%.

gems.name: Dioptase
gems.magical_effect: Dissolves in an already-enchanted liquid in 2 turns; each stone dissolved into such a liquid restores 1 hit point when drunk.

gems.name: Disthene
gems.magical_effect: Powdered ingredient in spell inks for controlled fiery effects (shaped flames, not explosive).

gems.name: Emerald
gems.magical_effect: Used in fertility, health, growth, and lie-detection spells and items. Worn on flesh directly contacting the flesh of a living deceiver: shatters to reveal the falsehood (does not trigger on the wearer's own lies). When mounted on healing or growth items: +2 bonus to all those item's saving throws; adds 2d4 extra charges; item spontaneously recharges (1 charge on a 5–6 on 1d6 each night). Use at waterclock (2 p.m.) for 20% better odds.
gems.notes: Kings wear emerald rings at parleys to detect treachery without a spell.

gems.name: Epidote
gems.magical_effect: Ingredient in potions of undead control and in protection-from-undead scroll inks.

gems.name: Euclase
gems.magical_effect: If a spell is cast on one or on a bearer: automatically triggers a flame strike effect (6d8/3d8 on save), consuming the gem.

gems.name: Eye Agate
gems.magical_effect: Powdered in sleeping drafts.
gems.incorrect_belief: Powder does not actually improve sleep drafts' effectiveness.

gems.name: Fire Agate
gems.magical_effect: Whole stones dissolved in fire lizard or pyrolisk blood: most favored base for potions of fire resistance.

gems.name: Fire Opal
gems.magical_effect: Used in items that cause, release, or control fire; essential in helms of brilliance. A whole mounted fire opal adds 1 point per die to damage done by any fire-producing magical item it adorns (not cumulative with multiple fire opals).

gems.name: Flamedance
gems.magical_effect: Stone and items set with it automatically succeed at all saves vs. normal and magical fire. Beings wearing one or more flamedance gems: +3 bonus to all fire-related saving throws.
gems.notes: Very rare; hard; ideal for carving.

gems.name: Fluorspar
gems.magical_effect: All forms, including Archon/Blue John: glows with a faint greenish radiance when magically invisible (not merely disguised or ethereal) objects or creatures come within 20 feet.
gems.notes: Pink/red varieties ("cabra stones") are the rare, more valuable type.

gems.name: Frost Agate
gems.magical_effect: Polyhedron-cut versions often become luckstones. Powder in potions: ensures peaceful miscibility — removes any chance of explosion or of a failed potion being poisonous.
gems.notes: Skilled cutting required to produce faceted version without splitting.

gems.name: Garnet
gems.magical_effect: Properly enchanted weapons set with garnets deal double or triple normal damage. Enchantments should commence at high morn (half-hour centered on 11 a.m.).
gems.incorrect_belief: Generally considered useless in magical work.
gems.notes: Thought by some fading faiths to be divine avatar's hardened blood.

gems.name: Gold Sheen
gems.magical_effect: Added to any spell creating radiance: caster precisely controls the spell's color. Added to invisibility magics: increases duration by 1d3 rounds.
gems.notes: Also see Sheen (the broader obsidian variety).

gems.name: Goldline
gems.magical_effect: Consumed in open flame with the right spells: a relatively easy way to give a bladed metal weapon a bonus enchantment.

gems.name: Greenstone
gems.magical_effect: Finest stones enchanted into greenstone amulets: wearer is immune to many mind-influencing spells (as ongoing mind blank). Powdered: component in spells resisting mental attacks and protective barriers. Can be transformed into an ioun stone.
gems.incorrect_belief: Nystul's magic aura is often used on cheap stones to fake valuable amulets.
gems.notes: Powdered greenstone must be used with care; reports of it completely negating some spells. Nine Secrets material

gems.name: Hambergyle
gems.magical_effect: Held in a flame while a light spell is pronounced over it: creates a continual light effect at the cost of the gem, which vaporizes.

gems.name: Heliodor
gems.magical_effect: Component in all priest sun-sphere spells in place of missing components (provided they need not be specially constructed). Essential ingredient in forging a sun blade.

gems.name: Hematite
gems.magical_effect: Strong magical affinity with blood and life forces; especially responsive to healing and necromancy enchantments. Used in periapts of healing and periapts of foul rotting. Can be transformed into an ioun stone.
gems.notes: Nine Secrets material

gems.name: Horn Coral
gems.magical_effect: Wearer who touches it with one of their own tears gains the ability to water walk (as the 3rd-level priest spell) for up to 6 turns; gem dissolves when the effect ends. Some special pieces become only inert for a turn and can then be reactivated.

gems.name: Hornbill Ivory
gems.magical_effect: Material component in spells and items concerned with flight.
gems.notes: From hornbill beaks, not true ivory.

gems.name: Hyaline
gems.magical_effect: Glows with a blue radiance when active magic takes effect, is launched, or passes within 20 feet.

gems.name: Hydrophane
gems.magical_effect: Used in water-oriented potions and items (water breathing, control water elementals). When used as an additional component in color spray: targets save at –1.
gems.notes: Opaque white when dry; transparent and iridescent when soaked in water.

gems.name: Hypersthene
gems.magical_effect: Wyvern warding: bearer is not seen or struck by a wyvern watch spell; they can pass through its warded area freely while the spell remains active.

gems.name: Iol
gems.magical_effect: Best gemstone type to transform into ioun stones (with the proper secret spells).
gems.notes: Commonly displays a color-change effect when viewed from different angles. Nine Secrets material

gems.name: Iris Agate
gems.magical_effect: Spell reflection: spells hurled at a screen or statue of iris agate rebound directly back at their source.
gems.notes: Sometimes placed as false guard statues or silhouettes in vault doorways.

gems.name: Irtios
gems.magical_effect: Prevents mildew, rot, and molds from affecting any organic substance in contact with it; protection includes yellow mold, mummy rot, and fungal diseases. Extends to a living or undead creature in continuous direct-flesh contact.

gems.name: Ivory
gems.magical_effect: Dragon teeth and fangs of certain magical creatures (such as displacer beasts) have magical uses; common beast ivory generally does not.
gems.notes: Unicorn horn (alicorn) is not ivory; commands thousands of gp from alchemists.

gems.name: Jacinth
gems.magical_effect: Ingredient in potions and items protecting against fire (rings of fire resistance). Has an inner flickering flame visible from afar (not bright enough to illuminate).
gems.notes: Found only in the Realms; other crystal spheres have an inferior garnet substitute.

gems.name: Jade
gems.magical_effect: Powdered: preferred base for spell inks for all illusion/phantasm spells; substitute for nonorganic components in all such castings. Essential ingredient in enchantment baths for illusion-capable items. Use in such processes initially at candleglass time (half-hour centered on 9 p.m.).
gems.incorrect_belief: Said to enhance musical ability — when certain simple enchantments are laid upon it, jade actually confers perfect pitch and sharp hearing to all who wear it.

gems.name: Jargoon
gems.magical_effect: Magic missile cast into a held jargoon: gem explodes (1d4+2 damage to caster), but the number of missiles in the spell is doubled. Missiles behave normally in all other respects.
gems.incorrect_belief: Falsely credited with preventing a lycanthrope from changing out of human form.

gems.name: Jasmal
gems.magical_effect: Hard enough to hold a cutting edge; can be worked into small nonmetallic weapons. In rows along a blade: holds multiple or complex enchantments that visit upon victims when the jasmals strike. Powdered: ingredient in enchantment baths for magical armor and in ink formulae for Veladar's Vambrace.

gems.name: Jasper
gems.magical_effect: Crushed: universal substitute ingredient in potions, antidotes, and items protecting against or neutralizing poison. Drinks stored in carved jasper vessels for at least a day are purged of all poisons, taints, and corrosive powers.
gems.notes: Preferred stone for both periapts of foul rotting and periapts of proof against poison.

gems.name: Jet
gems.magical_effect: Used in magic jars (favored gemstone). Certain treatments or spells cast too close to jet may free a long-imprisoned mage or creature from within — or summon a wizshade.
gems.incorrect_belief: Stone of mourning and sorrow; fell reputation partly due to magic jar use.

gems.name: Kings Tears
gems.magical_effect: Presence within 90 feet reduces casting time of legend lore to 2 turns and brings a name, word of activation, or key term regarding the subject into the caster's mind. A secret high-level ritual allows a spellcaster to permanently gain 1 point of Wisdom by sacrificing one. Can be cut into up to four gems of insight with proper enchantments.
gems.notes: Extremely rare; unique to the Realms; never yet cut, fractured, or chipped by any means. Each contains a vivid, unchanging scene from a long-dead ruler's life.

gems.name: Kornerupine
gems.magical_effect: Green variety only: if a magic mouth spell is cast on one and the last word left unsaid, it records all sounds within 20 ft for 4 rounds when the final word is later spoken. Records indefinitely; cannot be added to, silenced, or altered without shattering the stone.
gems.incorrect_belief: Brown variety has no known properties.

gems.name: Laeral's Tears
gems.magical_effect: Rarest of the nine secrets; can be transformed into an ioun stone. When prepared by a complex secret process known to Rashemani witches: absorbs all harm done to the wearer until the stone shatters — typically 24 points of damage before crumbling.
gems.notes: Nine Secrets material

gems.name: Lapis Lazuli
gems.magical_effect: Best gemstone for a periapt of health if ruby is unavailable. Powdered: principal base ingredient in potions of heroism and super-heroism.
gems.notes: The deeper the blue, the more valuable.

gems.name: Lumachella
gems.magical_effect: Powdered: ingredient in spell inks and components for both water breathing and airy water spells.

gems.name: Luriyl
gems.magical_effect: Glows and vibrates slightly when touched by magical tracer or scrutiny (any scrying or clairaudience spell) — warns of unseen eavesdroppers.

gems.name: Luspeel
gems.magical_effect: Considered vital by many for properly tempering swords that will bear multiple enchantments.
gems.notes: Ferromagnetic; used in temple furnishings for dramatic effect.

gems.name: Lynx Eye
gems.magical_effect: Dissolved in griffon blood or tears of a catoblepas: forms either a base for all healing or necromantically helpful potions, or an alternative ingredient in Keoghtom's ointment.
gems.notes: Green-flash variety of labradorite.

gems.name: Malachite
gems.magical_effect: Component in priest elemental-sphere spells and wizard spells involving ice, cold, fire, and heat. Powdered: ingredient in enchantment baths for items of warmth, fire resistance, and cold resistance.
gems.incorrect_belief: Falsely rumored to prevent falls.
gems.notes: Often set on rings of feather falling to exploit the false rumor for sales.

gems.name: Malacon
gems.magical_effect: Unique magical trap/delay: a spell can be cast into a malacon for later release in one of three ways — when dropped or struck; when the caster wills it forth (gem vaporizes); or at a preset time (gem dwindles). Specialized spells are needed to call forth a malacon's magic if one is not the original caster.

gems.name: Marble
gems.magical_effect: Magically inert (so far as is known).

gems.name: Meerschaum
gems.magical_effect: Can be converted into bone replacements by the stretchbone wizard spell, becoming indistinguishable from real bone for purposes of animate dead or similar magic.
gems.notes: Rumors of clairaudience and wizard eye casting through prepared distant meerschaum, and of necromantic uses, remain unconfirmed.

gems.name: Mellochrysos
gems.magical_effect: If held in open flame within a day of a light spell being cast on it: a single flame rises from the stone and burns for up to 12 hours, dwindling the stone away slowly. The flame is not extinguished by wind or water (even full immersion). Can be thrown to start long-duration fires in hard-to-reach places. Counter: phenalope.

gems.name: Microcline
gems.magical_effect: Powdered and dissolved in sap of any deciduous tree: most versatile and abundant alternative to octopus/squid ink as a base for spell inks.

gems.name: Moonbar
gems.magical_effect: Powdered: used in ink formulae, potions, and spell components for magic controlling, healing, or creating undead; can replace important missing ingredients related to necromancy.
gems.notes: Naturally large rectangular crystals with smooth surfaces.

gems.name: Moonstone
gems.magical_effect: True uses: powdered, component in abjuration and barrier spells; in evocation spells, used as a magical storage medium and for sudden energy redirection. Moonstones can substitute for many nonorganic abjuration/evocation components.
gems.incorrect_belief: Falsely said to force lycanthropes into animal form when seen.
gems.notes: Considered sacred to Selûne. Glows faintly for about an hour in darkness after light is removed.

gems.name: Moss Agate
gems.magical_effect: Ground fine: ingredient in medicines inducing enforced deep sleep; in all potions, causes normally incompatible substances to mix stably — always a safe additive, removing any chance of explosive or poisonous potion failure.

gems.name: Mykaro
gems.magical_effect: Cures blindness when powdered, mixed with any nonalcoholic drink, a wizard eye spell's viewing component is passed through the mixture, and the afflicted being drinks within 1 turn. Effect in 1d4+1 rounds (longer if eyeballs must regenerate).

gems.name: Mynteer
gems.magical_effect: Spell ink ingredient for levitation, telekinesis, and force-construct spells (unseen servant, Tenser's floating disc, etc.).

gems.name: Nelvine
gems.magical_effect: Spell and ink component in magics that disguise or change appearance without altering true nature.

gems.name: Nune
gems.magical_effect: Powdered ingredient in dispel magic spell ink; used in the bath during formative enchantment of a wand of negation.
gems.notes: Cross-shaped crystals up to 1 inch across.

gems.name: Obsidian
gems.magical_effect: Material component in spells emulating the priestly blade barrier spell; used in obsidian steed figurines. Best known of the nine secrets; can be transformed into an ioun stone.
gems.notes: Too fragile for most other magical uses. Nine Secrets material

gems.name: Octel
gems.magical_effect: When touched to a ring of free action, becomes "awakened" — glows bright enough to illuminate 2 ft in darkness and permanently prevents all paralyzation and hold magics from affecting anyone touching or bearing it.
gems.notes: The awakened property is permanent once gained.

gems.name: Onyx
gems.magical_effect: Contact with onyx aids in safe, relatively painless childbirths. Can be transformed into an ioun stone. Any unenchanted amount of onyx on a being: –1 penalty to all saves and ability checks.
gems.incorrect_belief: Generally considered unlucky.
gems.notes: Nine Secrets material

gems.name: Oolite
gems.magical_effect: Powdered: ingredient in castings and spell inks of purification and neutralization magics.
gems.notes: Too small to cut; usually polished and mounted in patterns.

gems.name: Opal
gems.magical_effect: Near-universal component in items that store spells for later release without loss of efficacy. Can replace missing components when other components are lacking. Never use in items that invoke both fire and lightning — immediately causes a chain lightning (12d6)-equivalent explosion that spawns Melf's minute meteors at each new target. Best used at twilight (6 p.m.); using it then increases enchanting odds by 2 or 25%.

gems.name: Ophealine
gems.magical_effect: When worn: prevents all magical hold spells and paralyzations. Warning: so deadening to magic that it cannot itself be used in any castings or spell preparations — the magic fails.
gems.notes: Called "knuckle stones" on Waterdeep streets; often sharpened and worn as a punching weapon.

gems.name: Orbaline
gems.magical_effect: Renders objects (not living things or undead) in contact with it resistant to fire: +4 bonus to item saves vs. normal fire, +5 vs. magical fire.

gems.name: Orblen
gems.magical_effect: If a healing spell is cast into it: radiates warmth and golden light in a 60-ft radius for 12 turns; beings in the radiance gain potion of vitality effects; remaining 6+ consecutive turns also cures 2d6 damage. If an invocation/evocation or combat-sphere spell is cast into it: explodes as a triple-strength meteor swarm (twelve 2-ft-diameter spheres, 10d4 damage each, 20 ft in all directions).

gems.name: Orl
gems.magical_effect: See Black Opal — same explosive combination: powdered orl + powdered black opal + open flame = the explosion described under Black Opal.
gems.notes: Red-hued orls are most valued.

gems.name: Orprase
gems.magical_effect: Powdered and mixed with wine consecrated to Tymora by a full priest of the goddess (at least 3 oz liquid + 1 stone): imbiber gains +6 bonus to their next save or ability check, however far in the future.
gems.notes: In high demand among Tymora's faithful.

gems.name: Pearl
gems.magical_effect: Material component of spells transforming acids into harmless water and of neutralize poison. Basis for pearl of power, pearl of the sirines, and pearl of wisdom. Powdered: valued in enchanting all magical mirrors.
gems.notes: Rare rainbow and black pearls are most valuable.

gems.name: Peridot
gems.magical_effect: Used in abjuration spells and protective items: one peridot per spell level (consumed) provides the equivalent of a proper component for casting or warding.

gems.name: Phenalope
gems.magical_effect: Prohibits all magical flames (including fireballs) from igniting or remaining alight within 60 ft — manifests as a momentary flash and puff of smoke only. Also extinguishes nonmagical fires (6-in-8 chance per round; 4-in-8 for oil-based fires); prevents reignition.
gems.notes: Found in palace floor mosaics for protection.

gems.name: Pipestone
gems.magical_effect: Can substitute for wood in any wizard (not priest) spell.

gems.name: Psaedros
gems.magical_effect: A hand-sized or larger mass can replace both the fire and holy water as material components of a wind walk spell.
gems.notes: Colors fade with prolonged sunlight.

gems.name: Rainbow Obsidian
gems.magical_effect: Pass stone for prismatic magics: can pierce shells of prismatic spells without triggering them or being harmed, and can bring inorganic materials attached to it through as well. Living creatures and undead wearing it still face normal prismatic effects.

gems.name: Raindrop
gems.magical_effect: See also Woodtine. Temporarily darkens when touched to any gemstone, metal, or stone that bore a deliberate enchantment but no longer does — more sensitive than detection spells, which only reveal the strongest residual enchantments.

gems.name: Ravenar
gems.magical_effect: Shares the tourmaline property: any spell of any level or class cast into a ravenar is transformed into three 6d6 straight-line lightning bolts radiating in directions chosen by the caster; consumes the gem.
gems.notes: Also see Tourmaline (all varieties share this property).

gems.name: Red Tears
gems.magical_effect: Universal substitute for all material components of healing spells (if not specially constructed); ingredient in inks for mending-object spells.
gems.notes: Teardrop-shaped, cherry-red, blood-crimson, or fiery orange crystals.

gems.name: Rhodochrosite
gems.magical_effect: Powdered in a special tea (full eyeball-sized stone): 20% chance of acting as neutralize poison or cure disease; entire batch must be consumed by one being.

gems.name: Rock Crystal
gems.magical_effect: Common component in spells requiring gemstone material of a stated value without specifying the type. When treated with two minor secret spells plus Veladar's Vambrace: becomes fusible like glass, then solidifies harder than normal — usable for mace heads, climbing spikes, or spear/ram heads.

gems.name: Rogue Stone
gems.magical_effect: Increases all chances of magic going wild, going wrong, or magic-related saving throw failures by 1 per stone within 20 ft (cumulative if multiple stones are together). Used in the gemjump spell.
gems.incorrect_belief: Primitive tribes believe them to be sentient dragon or hero essences.
gems.notes: Always found as singletons; no two rogue stones in one place at once; origin rock type unknown.

gems.name: Rosaline
gems.magical_effect: Trichroic crystals with the right color combination (rare): each crystal consumed negates one layer of a prismatic spell (outermost first). Identifying which crystals work is a deadly process that consumes the stone during testing.
gems.notes: Most rosaline crystals do not have the right nature; identifying the correct ones is itself dangerous.

gems.name: Ruby
gems.magical_effect: All items concerned with improving personal fortune (augmenting ability checks, saves, and survival rolls) can be made with +25% chance of enchanting succeeding if one ruby per function is powdered into the process (+10% if only one ruby for a multi-function item). Ruby dust widely used in sun-sphere and elemental priest spells and abjuration, alteration, and evocation wizard spells. Best at summer sunset (~5 p.m., +2 or 25% to efficacy). Essential in a helm of brilliance; preferred for healing items.
gems.incorrect_belief: Generally considered lucky.
gems.notes: Can correctly ward lightning and earthquakes; in very rare cases, contain unknown living creatures released when the gem is carefully shattered.

gems.name: Rusteen
gems.magical_effect: Spell component for wall of force and forcecage magics.

gems.name: Saganite
gems.magical_effect: Added to components of any spell with direct explosion or burst-of-flame effects: augments damage by 1 point per die.

gems.name: Samarskite
gems.magical_effect: Reduces all damage done by undead attacks by 1 point per attack (or per die of damage for multi-die attacks) for any being wearing or carrying it.
gems.notes: Used as mourning gemstone.

gems.name: Sanidine
gems.magical_effect: Any piece the size of the caster's thumb or larger: sole spell component for all spells involving water or purification (if components need not be specially constructed).
gems.notes: Favored by Bedine and other desert nomadic peoples.

gems.name: Sapphire
gems.magical_effect: Widely used in items related to magical prowess, the mind, and the element of air. Wearer partially protected against fear, anger, despair, and insanity effects; +2 bonus to all saves vs. emotion/mind-clouding magic (charms, feeblemind, insanity) or a normal save when none would ordinarily be allowed. A whole sapphire (5,000+ gp) in an enchantment bath plus powdered sapphire: 55% chance of raising a weapon's magical bonus by 1. As spell component: spells last for the longest possible time and deal maximum damage in their first round. Best at midmorn (10 a.m.).

gems.name: Sarbossa
gems.magical_effect: Added to components of spells involving shape transformation of a victim: adds 1d2 rounds to spell duration.
gems.notes: Found in nodules up to 1 inch in volcanic cavities.

gems.name: Sardonyx
gems.magical_effect: Used in spells and items affecting Wisdom. Same magical uses as kings tears. Can be transformed into an ioun stone. Sardonyx gemstones sometimes (not reliably) guard against magic missile: 2-in-6 chance of absorbing 1 point of damage per missile (not per spell); gem is never harmed.
gems.notes: Nine Secrets material

gems.name: Satin Spar
gems.magical_effect: Partially negates magic missiles: any missile aimed at the bearer vaporizes a satin spar stone worn/carried/touched, but deals only half damage.
gems.notes: Too fragile to wear normally.

gems.name: Scapra
gems.magical_effect: When added to components of a guards and wards spell (consumed in casting): permits addition of either one extra magical effect beyond the normal five, or one phantasmal force effect. One extra effect per gemstone, maximum five additions.

gems.name: Serpentine
gems.magical_effect: Each stone (gemstone or the right hardstone variety) functions once against cold and once against fire as the priestly resist fire or resist cold spell, then crumbles. Multiple serpentines on one bearer: only one activates per trigger event.
gems.incorrect_belief: Malachite is falsely rumored to prevent falls; serpentine is actually the fire/cold protection stone.
gems.notes: Only jewelers, expert miners (most dwarves), and experienced wizards or priests can reliably identify the magically active variety from inert serpentine.

gems.name: Shandon
gems.magical_effect: When an ironguard spell is cast on one shandon already affixed to a garment that has at least six other shandons: the ironguard effect becomes permanent to the garment. Metal does not catch on the garment and poisons from metal weapons still take effect. Ends if the enspelled shandon is crushed, shattered, or separated from the garment.
gems.notes: Tiny; colorless; too small to impress untrained observers.

gems.name: Sharpstone
gems.magical_effect: Any amount consumed in a casting increases the radius of spell effects by 10 ft at the cost of 1 die of damage (or 1 round of duration for spells without damage). Multiple stones or large amounts cannot stack.

gems.name: Sheen
gems.magical_effect: Sheen (all varieties) added to spells creating radiance: caster precisely controls the spell's color. When added to invisibility magics: +1d3 rounds of duration.
gems.notes: Gold sheen is a semiprecious gem-grade variety; most other sheens are ornamental. Both share these properties.

gems.name: Shou Lung Amethyst
gems.magical_effect: Used to protect noblemen in Kara-Tur; puissant magical powers otherwise unknown to Faerûnian wizards.
gems.notes: Eastern import; deep purple corundum.

gems.name: Shou Lung Emerald
gems.magical_effect: Harder and more lustrous than Faerûnian emerald; little is known of its magical properties in the West.
gems.incorrect_belief: Legend says only three exist; at least a dozen caches are known in the West, discrediting this.

gems.name: Shou Lung Topaz
gems.magical_effect: Reputed magical properties unknown to Faerûnian wizards; often used in items associated with felines.
gems.notes: Eastern import; fiery yellow corundum.

gems.name: Silkstone
gems.magical_effect: Powdered: reliable substitute component in spells and inks for life-energy draining and restoration. Worn around the neck: shadows (undead) always hesitate for 1 round when confronting a bearer — they will not attack in that round, but will if the bearer attacks them.
gems.incorrect_belief: Falsely said to ward off spirits generally.

gems.name: Sinhalite
gems.magical_effect: No sort of magical darkness can form or persist within 20 feet of a sinhalite.
gems.notes: Found only in streambed or vanished-stream gravels.

gems.name: Skydrop
gems.magical_effect: Renders any being touching, carrying, or wearing it immune to petrification.
gems.notes: Meteoritic glass from desert gravel fields.

gems.name: Smoky Quartz
gems.magical_effect: The black morion variety only: used in necromantic and necromancy spell inks and bone-strengthening baths; makes bone as hard as steel and renders it immune to hostile necromancies.
gems.notes: Much of what is called cairngorm is actually heat-colored glass.

gems.name: Snowflake Obsidian
gems.magical_effect: A thumbnail-sized or larger piece worn/carried on an outer surface reduces dragon breath weapon damage by 1d4 points per die (minimum 1 per die). Consumed in doing so; no effect on breath weapon transformations or incidental effects.

gems.name: Soapstone
gems.magical_effect: Reputed to have magical properties related to fire and capture of warmth; as yet a mystery.

gems.name: Sphene
gems.magical_effect: Wards off lightning (including from spells): saving throws vs. lightning +4 bonus; damage rolls –1 point per die.
gems.incorrect_belief: Little known outside specialized circles.

gems.name: Spinel
gems.magical_effect: Specially crushed and ingested: allows any spellcasting being to instantly recall the last spell it cast.

gems.name: Spodumene
gems.magical_effect: Opens wizard lock doors and items on contact, provided it is sprinkled with at least three drops of holy water (water is consumed; gem is not).
gems.notes: Kunzite fades in color over time — faded form called ghost stone.

gems.name: Star Diopside
gems.magical_effect: Winks and flashes vigorously when any active illusion/phantasm magic (a magically disguised person) passes within 10 feet.
gems.notes: Stones with a four- or six-rayed star are the valuable variety.

gems.name: Star Metal
gems.magical_effect: Combined in small amounts with alloys: adds sharpness and flexible temper to bladed weapons; reputedly heightens strength and duration of all enchantments in blades containing it. Valued in the thousands of gp per workable chunk.
gems.notes: Most specimens are thumb-sized or smaller.

gems.name: Star Rose Quartz
gems.magical_effect: Alternative spell component in all abjuration wizard spells and protection-sphere priest spells (if components need not be specially constructed). When worn or carried: 14% chance of magically redirecting a spell aimed at the bearer to some other target.

gems.name: Star Ruby
gems.magical_effect: If a wraithform spell is cast on one that has already received a knock spell: becomes a thick red vapor. Inhaled by a mammalian being: combines the effects of an elixir of health, a regeneration spell, and a heal spell. Cannot raise the dead but restores the recently revived to full vitality.
gems.notes: 1 in 100 rubies is a star ruby.

gems.name: Star Sapphire
gems.magical_effect: Material component of minor globe of invulnerability or globe of invulnerability — each case raises the spell level of spells warded off by 1. Used in antimagic shell (normally no component needed): increases duration by 14 turns and maintains it during the caster's sleep. Many other uses in protective items.
gems.notes: 1 in 1,000 sapphires is a star sapphire.

gems.name: Sulabra
gems.magical_effect: Magically inert (so far as is known).

gems.name: Sunstone
gems.magical_effect: Stores light-related and energy-discharge magics for later release; activator touches the stone and speaks the last word of the spell incantation to discharge it at a chosen target (or random target if the activator did not concentrate). Activation destroys the stone. Need not be the original caster to activate.

gems.name: Tabasheer
gems.magical_effect: Crushed and a cure light wounds spell cast on the powder while on the tongue or in an open wound of a being: grants 3d6 temporary hit points for 24 hours. Damage is taken from these phantom hit points first; each lost is gone permanently. Does not increase level, spell abilities, or anything else.
gems.notes: Found in joints of certain bamboo varieties.

gems.name: Tchazar
gems.magical_effect: In any cut: clouds scrying magics from seeing anything within 2 feet of it. Frequently used on coffers, collars, reading desks, locks, and bracers. Power is instantly lost if the stone shatters.

gems.name: Tempskya
gems.magical_effect: Alternative material component in all spells concerned with petrification and enchantments for items concerning petrification.

gems.name: Thuparlial
gems.magical_effect: Powdered: ingredient in spell ink formulae and casting components for pyrotechnics and heat metal spells.
gems.notes: Red Wizards experiment with using it as a fire-spell replacement component; no success reported.

gems.name: Tiger Eye Agate
gems.magical_effect: Powdered: commercially expected in potions of undead control and tomb/death inscription inks — market demand persists despite no true magical property.
gems.incorrect_belief: Falsely said to repel spirits and undead.
gems.notes: Buyers expect it; alchemists include it; it does nothing.

gems.name: Tomb Jade
gems.magical_effect: Powdered: ingredient in potions of undead control. Brandished by a priest who has already failed a turning attempt: allows a second turning attempt at +1 bonus.
gems.notes: Jade reddened or browned through burial. Jade turned green by nearby buried bronze is no more valuable than normal jade.

gems.name: Topaz
gems.magical_effect: Prolongs faerie fire spells cast upon it to last 6d4 days. Ensures the item it is mounted on is immune to breakage or change of state (disintegration, petrification, melting, corrosion). Best gemstone for a gem of brightness (enchantments make it as hard as mithral). Naturally stores any healing spell cast on it; released by placing the gem into an open wound (melts away) or powdering it and drinking in milk or wine from a mithral goblet.

gems.name: Tourmaline
gems.magical_effect: Any spell of any level or class cast into a tourmaline is transformed into three 6d6 straight-line lightning bolts in directions chosen by the caster, consuming the tourmaline. Black variety (ravenar) is a gem-grade stone; all other hues share this property as fancy-grade stones.

gems.name: Tremair
gems.magical_effect: Worn next to skin: makes the wearer immune to all magical curses.
gems.notes: Sometimes sewn onto debutantes' gowns to signal availability.

gems.name: Turquoise
gems.magical_effect: Used in enchantment baths for flight items; best worked at foredawn (half-hour centered on 5 a.m.). Grants stability in flight (despite wind disturbances) to items enchanted with it.
gems.incorrect_belief: Gleaming near gold is thought to bring prosperity (folk belief). Turquoise sliver in a horse's harness said to bring good luck and protection (folk belief).
gems.notes: Elves prize specimens without mottlings for sky-related spells.

gems.name: Turritella
gems.magical_effect: Magically inert (so far as is known, despite much speculation).
gems.notes: Dark brown agate with silicified spiral shells.

gems.name: Ulvaen
gems.magical_effect: Touched to an open wound or placed on the tongue (for internal injuries): melts away in 1d4+1 rounds and heals in sequence. Roll 1d4 repeatedly: 1 = stops and heals 2d4 (first roll), 1d6+1 (second), 1d4+1 (third), or 1d10 (fourth) damage, ending the stone's work; any other result advances to the next healing stage (stop bleeding → restore organs → close wounds → full regeneration).

gems.name: Variscite
gems.magical_effect: Poisonous to lycanthropes. Mounted on an arrowtip or blade: triples damage on first strike against a particular lycanthrope (no further damage from that variscite to that individual for one day). Worn as a gemstone: can deal 1d6+4 damage once if pressed into an open wound on a lycanthrope or put in contact with their tongue (must reach the bloodstream).

gems.name: Violine
gems.magical_effect: Upon contact with a being with mummy rot: consumed but negates the mummy rot. A mummy brought into contact with any amount of violine: suffers 4d4 damage. If the mummy is destroyed, the resulting dust is ineffective for magical uses.

gems.name: Water Opal
gems.magical_effect: Used in crafting magical scrying devices (crystal balls). Powdered and mixed with holy water: creates an elixir of health without any enchantments needed.
gems.notes: Clear, translucent; iridescent color play.

gems.name: Waterstar
gems.magical_effect: Shares tourmaline property: any spell cast into it transforms into three 6d6 straight-line lightning bolts, consuming the stone.
gems.notes: Must be entirely free of flaws; yields large faceted gemstones.

gems.name: Webstone
gems.magical_effect: When carried in direct flesh-to-stone contact: protects the bearer from all harmful gaseous and airborne particulate effects (smoke, poisonous gases, airborne fungal spores). Each contact with such things partially vaporizes the stone at a variable rate. Protection varies wildly from specimen to specimen.

gems.name: Witherite
gems.magical_effect: When set in a special electrum setting and worn in direct flesh-to-stone contact: provides immunity to withering magics, psionic withering, and the reversed damaging form of necromantic sphere priest spells.

gems.name: Wonderstone
gems.magical_effect: Glows with eerie blue-green or deep royal blue radiance for 5d4 rounds after direct contact with a spell effect, magical item, or any being or item bearing an active enchantment.
gems.notes: Used as magic detectors at entryways; also popular in wealthy furniture for mood lighting.

gems.name: Woodtine
gems.magical_effect: Shares raindrop's property: temporarily darkens when touched to any gem, metal, or stone that once bore a deliberate enchantment but no longer does. More sensitive than most detection spells.
gems.notes: Brown fibrous variety of cassiterite; a corruption of "wood tin."

gems.name: Xylopal
gems.magical_effect: A hand-sized piece or collection of fragments can replace both the lodestone and iron filings in casting the 7th-level wizard spell reverse gravity.

gems.name: Zarbrina
gems.magical_effect: Powdered: acceptable alternative ingredient in spell inks for illusion magic.

gems.name: Zendalure
gems.magical_effect: Powdered and mixed with water: creates "seasonsteal," a glycerine-like perfect preservative that keeps mammalian, reptilian, or avian parts completely undecayed indefinitely, so long as fully immersed and kept from direct sunlight. Remains stored this way are considered fresh for healing magics and other magical processes.

gems.name: Ziose
gems.magical_effect: Unleashes six magic missile pulses (1d4+1 each) per round for up to seven continuous rounds, activated by the last intelligent being to touch it, at will, up to 30 ft distance; no concentration needed. After seven rounds, falls inert for 2 turns. If never used for seven continuous rounds, no rest period required.

gems.name: Zircon
gems.magical_effect: Takes enchantments readily; one of the favorite base stones for gem, scarab, or eye magical items (cut into cusps).
gems.incorrect_belief: Occasionally passed off as more valuable stones.
gems.notes: Anyone with gemcutting knowledge can tell the difference.

gems.name: Adamant
gems.description: Made only by Celebrimbor among the High Jewel Smiths. Harder than diamond or laen, yet colorable like laen and faceted like diamond — clear, brilliant, brighter than diamond. Used as the setting-stone of Nenya, Galadriel's Ring.

gems.name: Diamond
gems.description: Most prized by Men and Dwarves; the Mírdain find white stones "dull." Elves covet the very scarce colored varieties, especially blues and pale violets.

gems.name: Emerald
gems.description: Called "Elfstones" by mortals; favored by the Firstborn for their bright green color, often set in jewelry.

gems.name: Laen
gems.description: Crystal lattice structure gives great strength. Gains rigidity with heat; must be chilled to temperatures beyond cold to soften and sculpt. Natural laen is black or smoky; can be cleared and tinted any transparent color.

gems.name: Opal
gems.description: Cloudy, rainbow-hued; favored by Elves for rings and weapon pommels. Fire Opal (red-blue-violet) highly prized; Black Opal rarer still and uniquely beautiful.

gems.name: Ruby
gems.description: Favorite stone of Noldorin smiths (used in Narya, one of the Three). Richest dark reds preferred by Elves; Men prefer brighter shades; Morgoth/Sauron's servants favor dark blood-reds or cloudy varieties.

gems.name: Sapphire
gems.description: Pure blue most prized by Elves (used in Vilya, one of the Three); yellow variety also valued. Black Sapphire very rare and ominous.

gems.name: Violet Garnet
gems.description: The only garnet taken seriously by the Noldor — clear pale violet, delicate and beautiful. Dwarves enjoy common dark reds; Men use most varieties, preferring violet; brown-green varieties favored in the south. Often found in large clumps of interlocking crystals.

herbs.name: Akbutege
herbs.effect: Eating the leaf heals 1–10 hits.
herbs.notes: Laurel-family shrub, southern wetlands.

herbs.name: Alambas
herbs.effect: Crushed-grass juice heals 4 sq ft of even 3rd-degree burns.
herbs.notes: Succulent grass.

herbs.name: Aloe
herbs.effect: Juice heals 1–4 hits (5/dose for burns); only 20% effective on major wounds; doubles minor cut/burn healing rate; mild anesthetic.
herbs.notes: Cultivated in gardens in the North.

herbs.name: Arfandas
herbs.effect: Poultice doubles fracture-healing rate.
herbs.notes: Juice cannot be preserved.

herbs.name: Arlan
herbs.effect: Poultice cures 1–6 (wild) or 4–9 (domestic) hits of bruise/concussion; root is a decongestant (+20 RR vs. colds, 5x respiratory recovery).
herbs.notes: Species debated alongside Arlian's Slipper.

herbs.name: Arlian's Slipper
herbs.effect: Boiled root vapor: +20 RR vs. cold, 5x respiratory recovery rate.
herbs.notes: Considered by some the same species as Arlan.

herbs.name: Arnuminas
herbs.effect: Doubles healing rate for bruises, sprains, and pulled tendons; reduces swelling.
herbs.notes: Dried/salve form less effective than fresh.

herbs.name: Arunya
herbs.effect: Root juice causes deep sleep; 1 hour of sleep equals 4 hours' rest; used in surgery as an anaesthetic.
herbs.notes: Addictive after 2+ consecutive days of use.

herbs.name: Asp Glands
herbs.effect: Large doses (2–3) are a powerful organ restorer.
herbs.notes: Side effect: fits of madness recurring over the following days.

herbs.name: Athelas
herbs.effect: Eases pain and mental suffering; cures diseases; neutralizes minor poisons; defeats the Black Breath; slows major poisons; triples healing rate on any wound.
herbs.notes: By the late Third Age, Gondorians believed it had only a pleasant scent and mild headache-curing use, having forgotten its true power. Power is "seemingly unbounded" in the hands of a rightful King.

herbs.name: Attanar
herbs.effect: Poultice reduces fever.
herbs.notes: Streamside moss.

herbs.name: Avhail
herbs.effect: Fruit is the base ingredient of biotaille brandy.
herbs.notes: No direct healing effect.

herbs.name: Balaak
herbs.effect: 4 oz dose heals even the most badly shattered bone.
herbs.notes: Tidal-marsh reed.

herbs.name: Barani
herbs.effect: Tea reduces nausea and vomiting.
herbs.notes: Common wild ground plant.

herbs.name: Black Clover
herbs.effect: Poison. Pollen causes burning lungs, coughing, vomiting; prolonged exposure can kill.
herbs.notes: Refined into Drúedain hunting-dart poison.

herbs.name: Black Vines
herbs.effect: Poison. Contact causes euphoric paralysis while the vine smothers the victim; death in 2–20 rounds unless aided.

herbs.name: Bodezlist
herbs.effect: Heart-tissue water source equal to a day's water ration.
herbs.notes: The plant's 1–6 or 1–10+20 dagger-equivalent cuts to anyone blundering in are a real hazard, not a folk belief.

herbs.name: Bog-land Grass
herbs.effect: Fibers woven into waterproof rope/baskets.
herbs.notes: Invasive marsh weed; no medicinal use.

herbs.name: Blue Pine
herbs.effect: Edible seeds (pine nuts), minor nutrition.
herbs.notes: Wood valued separately for tannic-acid preservative qualities (see Woods).

herbs.name: Boneset
herbs.effect: Triples fracture-healing rate (root, fresh or dried).
herbs.notes: Multiple doses do not stack.

herbs.name: Boskone
herbs.effect: Inhaled powder grants heightened/Awareness senses for 10–20 rounds.
herbs.notes: Highly addictive; severe headache (–30) follows for hours.

herbs.name: Bright Blue Eyes
herbs.effect: Tea from 25 flowers grants Elf-sharp vision for 3 hours, once per day.
herbs.notes: Cannot be stored without losing potency.

herbs.name: Caj
herbs.effect: Tea halves spellcaster Power Point recovery time for 2 days.
herbs.notes: 5% cumulative monthly chance of fatal "Long Path" euphoric death-wish.

herbs.name: Carefree Mustard
herbs.effect: Seed plaster heals superficial wounds within an hour; soothes deeper pain.
herbs.notes: Seeds store; plaster must be used immediately.

herbs.name: Cicino
herbs.effect: +75 disease RR for Ents/Huorns/Trees; +40 for humans.
herbs.notes: Must soak 10 days in mineral spring water first.

herbs.name: Coraco
herbs.effect: Juice heals 2–20 hits (8 oz dose).
herbs.notes: Labor-intensive to harvest.

herbs.name: Craeg-cerflun
herbs.effect: Poison/petrification. Boiled root/leaf juice or flower mist; effects range from sleep to coma to partial/total petrification depending on RR result.

herbs.name: Culan
herbs.effect: Antispasmodic; reduces certain poison effects.
herbs.notes: Imported powder/tincture.

herbs.name: Curfalaka
herbs.effect: Fruit heals muscle injuries.
herbs.notes: Swamp-jungle shrub.

herbs.name: Darsurion
herbs.effect: Rubbed leaf heals 1–6 hits (concussion).
herbs.notes: Rocky-slope shrub.

herbs.name: Deadly Milk-White Trumpet
herbs.effect: Poison. Pollen causes blindness/nausea/madness; seeds cause battle-euphoria (1 seed) up to lethal doses (kills Men/Hobbits at 2+, Dwarves at 3+, Orcs at 10+; Elves immune).

herbs.name: Delrean
herbs.effect: Leaf acts as insect repellent; attackers must RR vs. 7th-level shroud.
herbs.notes: Bark makes a pleasant drink.

herbs.name: Dragul
herbs.effect: Tea grants +10 to observation-based maneuvers for ~1 hour.
herbs.notes: Addictive with regular use; severe withdrawal.

herbs.name: Dwarves' Eyebright
herbs.effect: Tea grants +50 to dim/dark-condition sighting (up to 50' infravision for Men).
herbs.notes: Habitual users develop violet-tinted eye-whites.

herbs.name: Elbin's Basket
herbs.effect: Root extract doubles the drinker's action speed for 1 round.
herbs.notes: Difficult to extract.

herbs.name: Elendil's Basket
herbs.effect: Root liquid slows poison 10x; purifies foul water; effect lasts 12 hrs.
herbs.notes: Rare red tundra flower.

herbs.name: Eredena
herbs.effect: Buds spike heart rate, strength, speed, and thought.
herbs.notes: Genuinely dangerous: failed RR vs. 20th-level poison can cause fainting, heart attack, or death. Ents do not know its effect on humans.

herbs.name: Faghiu
herbs.effect: Love-potion juice; victim will not harm the giver for 1–100 days and will serve them faithfully.
herbs.notes: High-altitude flower.

herbs.name: Feduilas
herbs.effect: +20 RR vs. Mentalism/Essence attacks for 1–5 hours.
herbs.notes: –10 agility/quickness during effect; mildly addictive intoxicant.

herbs.name: Fleabane
herbs.effect: Repels bloodsucking insects and pests (95% fresh juice, 80% powder).

herbs.name: Frostheal
herbs.effect: Cures frostbite.
herbs.notes: High-altitude alpine herb.

herbs.name: Golden Cress
herbs.effect: Ointment closes and heals 1–5 hits of bleeding wounds in 1–5 rounds.
herbs.notes: Wound will not reopen once closed.

herbs.name: Gorfang
herbs.effect: Poison. Reddish mist causes sleep; juice can be fatal.

herbs.name: Gumumiti leaves
herbs.effect: Reduces stun duration by 3 rounds.
herbs.notes: From the teak tree (see Woods).

herbs.name: Haruella
herbs.effect: Used against the Undead (specific mechanic against wights).
herbs.notes: Formula is a deep secret.

herbs.name: Harwite
herbs.effect: Heals 10–50 hits when chewed; filter/ingredient in Ent Draughts.
herbs.notes: Forest-floor moss.

herbs.name: Healer's Chamomile
herbs.effect: Triples healing rate during 2–12 hour induced sleep.
herbs.notes: More than 2 doses in 3 days risks permanent impairment (01–25 chance per repeat dose). Patient wakes ravenous and irritable.

herbs.name: Hiam Moss
herbs.effect: Mood elevator; sustains one person a full day without food.
herbs.notes: 1–5% chance of fatal first-use allergic reaction; maximum 4 consecutive days' use.

herbs.name: Hopper Mushrooms
herbs.effect: Tea repairs any organ damage.
herbs.notes: Often confused with True Tarnas due to shared nickname. Causes 1–10 hours of nausea (–50) as a side effect.

herbs.name: Hrast
herbs.effect: Nourishing fruit; sustains a traveler nearly a full day.
herbs.notes: Least common of three Gaj tree species.

herbs.name: Karfar
herbs.effect: Poison. Pasty, lethal poison from Juha tree leaves; easy to apply to weapons or food.

herbs.name: Kelventari
herbs.effect: Berry juice heals 3rd-degree burns fully, lesser burns 1–10 hits; eliminates scarring.
herbs.notes: Rare; short fruiting season.

herbs.name: Kirtir
herbs.effect: +10 Quickness for 1 hour (with –5 Agility); can cause weight loss in smaller doses.
herbs.notes: After-effect: –30 Constitution bonus for 1–10 hours, total exhaustion; overdose risks hallucination/seizure/death.

herbs.name: Kiseoboba
herbs.effect: Numbs the sensation of thirst (does not replace actual water need).
herbs.notes: Users can mistakenly believe they no longer need water — a real, stated danger of the herb. 5th-level RR (Intuition-modified) to avoid the false confidence.

herbs.name: Klytun
herbs.effect: Poison. Root paste induces 1–10 day catatonic trance.

herbs.name: Lainimit leaves
herbs.effect: Reduces stun duration by 2 rounds.
herbs.notes: From the mahogany tree.

herbs.name: Latha
herbs.effect: +10 RR vs. disease; heals 12 hits.
herbs.notes: Mild analgesic; good for headaches and toothaches.

herbs.name: Lawrim
herbs.effect: Skin contact causes itchy rash/numbness; boiled and squeezed yields an oily level-2 poison causing shock then temporary paralysis.

herbs.name: Lemsang
herbs.effect: 1 lb feeds a person for a week.
herbs.notes: Associated in folk-tale with Lembas, but unrelated.

herbs.name: Lichen Gloriosa
herbs.effect: Sharpens blades to cut stone without resharpening.
herbs.notes: Must be used immediately on gathering; cannot be stored.

herbs.name: Lothfelag
herbs.effect: Preserves living tissue; absolves pain; can restore lost life.
herbs.notes: Exceptionally rare; subject of Dwarvish legend and verse.

herbs.name: Lothgalen / Loth Nenond
herbs.effect: Secretion (Nen Calgalen) is a deadly injected poison causing burning agony, paralysis, and sometimes death. Vines also make exceptionally strong rope.
herbs.notes: Dwarves generally scorn its use as a poison even in war.

herbs.name: Lus
herbs.effect: Poison. Fast-acting; first symptom is always blindness; severity scales from temporary blindness to death by RR margin.

herbs.name: Madarch
herbs.effect: Diluted juice heals all cuts/damaged blood vessels within 2 hours.
herbs.notes: Undiluted use reopens wounds and can cause fatal vein rupture — a real "more is worse" trap flagged in the text as a moral about greed.

herbs.name: Madwort
herbs.effect: Poison. Paste causes 11–20 rounds of madness; severe cases cause permanent Reasoning stat loss.

herbs.name: Melem Loza
herbs.effect: Halves 2nd-degree-or-less burn effects; doubles effect of healing magic used alongside it.
herbs.notes: Rare; difficult to distinguish from similar vines.

herbs.name: Mirenna
herbs.effect: Berry juice heals 10 hits instantly.
herbs.notes: Warriors carry one between cheek and teeth for emergency use.

herbs.name: Miretar's Crown
herbs.effect: Stops bleeding when laid across a wound.
herbs.notes: Rare high-meadow flower.

herbs.name: Nelthandon
herbs.effect: Powerful emetic, whether boiled or eaten raw.

herbs.name: Numenelos
herbs.effect: Nerve regeneration and repair.
herbs.notes: Moss from the White Tree's base at Fornost.

herbs.name: Phacalus
herbs.effect: Permanently raises Presence/Intuition/Intelligence (RM: Presence/Reasoning/Intuition/Empathy/Memory) by 1 each, up to stat cap.
herbs.notes: 35% chance of severe negative reaction per dose — toxic coma or allergic reaction ranging from rash to death.

herbs.name: Pipeweed
herbs.effect: Recreational smoking herb.
herbs.notes: Brought from Númenor; popularized in the Shire by Tobold "Old Toby" Hornblower c. T.A. 2700.

herbs.name: Rivertraveller
herbs.effect: Raises Presence for 2 hours (then –50 for 1–10 hours).
herbs.notes: Euphoric stimulant/hallucinogen; used in Breffraen chieftain-selection rites.

herbs.name: Rose Trees
herbs.effect: Nectar grants +25 to enchantment spells cast on a covered object; cleanses poison from the body.
herbs.notes: Hedges form impassable thorny barriers.

herbs.name: Sailchas
herbs.effect: +10 morale, +10 RR, +5 DB for 3–7 days while worn.
herbs.notes: Believed to be a harbinger of good luck by Cardolan folk.

herbs.name: Sarah-Pokes-Her-Head
herbs.effect: Aged root (1 lunar cycle) sustains 3 people for a week.
herbs.notes: Root is bitter and burning before aging — a real property, not a misconception. Related to jack-in-the-pulpit.

herbs.name: Sha
herbs.effect: Powder grants infravision (up to 300', 1–5 rounds at a time).
herbs.notes: Side effect: 1–5 days of severe diarrhea beginning 11–20 hours after use.

herbs.name: Silraen
herbs.effect: Powerful analgesic.
herbs.notes: Side effect: drowsiness.

herbs.name: Sindoluin
herbs.effect: Anti-coagulant tincture.
herbs.notes: Small blue flower.

herbs.name: Slird
herbs.effect: Poison. Fast-acting (level 2) circulatory poison; paralyzes 1–6 extremities for 1–100 days.
herbs.notes: Also listed under Woods (the Slird tree's fruit; see Section 6.5).

herbs.name: Splayfoot Goodwort
herbs.effect: Mashed seeds instill confidence and purpose in good characters.
herbs.notes: Causes dizziness/confusion (–50, 1–4 hours) specifically when given to evil beings — an intentional moral-alignment effect. Marsh plant near the Gladden Fields.

herbs.name: Suranie
herbs.effect: Berry relieves fainting (equivalent to 1-round stun relief).
herbs.notes: "Smelling salts" equivalent.

herbs.name: Sweet Sorrel
herbs.effect: Cures lung/throat/airway ailments; antidote to poisonous gases; relieves lung-spasms; breaks certain trance/sleep states (see White Mountain Poppy).

herbs.name: Tartec
herbs.effect: Refined Tartella — deeper euphoria at 1/4 dose.
herbs.notes: Permanently reduces Reasoning/Intelligence by 1 per dose; faster and worse addiction than Tartella.

herbs.name: Tartella
herbs.effect: Euphoric-relaxant; 1–10 hours of euphoria.
herbs.notes: Tolerance builds after 2–5 doses; severe withdrawal (nausea, headaches, chills, seizures).

herbs.name: Teldalion
herbs.effect: Poultice reduces inflammation.
herbs.notes: Found only in deep forests.

herbs.name: Touch-grass
herbs.effect: Changes shape on touch by different races for 1 hour (scouting/tracking tool).
herbs.notes: Inedible.

herbs.name: True Tarnas
herbs.effect: Boiled bulb heals any organ damage.
herbs.notes: Often confused with Hopper Mushrooms ("False Tarnas") due to shared common name. Only the dormant bulb has medicinal value, not the flower.

herbs.name: Tulaxar
herbs.effect: Styptic — stops all bleeding within 1–10 rounds.
herbs.notes: Healer's garden herb.

herbs.name: Tyr-fira
herbs.effect: Said to be life-restoring if given within 56 days of death.
herbs.notes: Possibly extinct by the book's present day — "purely a matter of conjecture" per the text.

herbs.name: White Lily
herbs.effect: Used to brew Meathran (Dunnish national drink); nectar used in Cranor manufacture (see Metals).

herbs.name: White Mountain Poppy
herbs.effect: Single dose: trance state, –100 all actions but doubles detection/information-spell range and effect. Double dose: deep aware sleep. Triple dose: 6–12 hour unwakeable sleep.
herbs.notes: Highly addictive. Sweet Sorrel breaks the trance in 4–10 rounds.

herbs.name: White-Berried Yew
herbs.effect: Poison when ripe. Historically used for honor-suicide; unripe berries merely induce vomiting.

herbs.name: Wight Orchid
herbs.effect: Root induces astral-projection-like trance (range 10 mi/level); spirit can pass non-magical barriers.
herbs.notes: Genuinely risky: RR failures can strand or "lose" the spirit, killing the body in 2–12 days.

herbs.name: Wild Persimmons
herbs.effect: Edible fruit, low nutrition (100 needed for a meal).
herbs.notes: Anduin Valley riverside tree.

herbs.name: Winclamit
herbs.effect: Heals 3–300 hits (boiled fruit).
herbs.notes: Does not thrive where timber has been heavily logged.

herbs.name: Witan
herbs.effect: Relieves 2 rounds of stun when swallowed.
herbs.notes: Causes excessive spitting as a side effect of chewing. Carried by fighters of the Bozishnarod.

herbs.name: Wolfstooth
herbs.effect: Poison. Root paste causes irregular heartbeat; moderate exposure damages Constitution (–15 to –20 temporary); severe exposure can cause fatal heart failure.

herbs.name: Yellow Hemlock
herbs.effect: Resin stops bleeding on contact immediately, any severity.
herbs.notes: Tree also listed in Section 6.5 (Woods); wood used for carving/laminating.

metals.name: Adamant
metals.magical_properties: Hardest substance on Toril but brittle. Shields against all fire and heat (magical or not): wearer strides through small fires unscathed; takes only 1d6 from fireball-equivalent exposure to exposed areas. Auto-succeeds vs. normal fire, cold, and electricity. +6 vs. magical fire. +4 vs. acid, disintegration, lightning. –4 vs. crushing blow and fall unless enchanted to compensate. Takes enchantments readily. Worth five times its weight in gold.
metals.notes: Jet black with rainbow-edged reflections. Brittle — sword of adamant would snap if struck. Best found in Waterdeep and the Great Rift. Styluses for engraving; dwarven experimental use only in larger items.

metals.name: Adamantine
metals.type: Alloy (5/8 adamant + 2/8 silver + 1/8 electrum, or mithral + steel in a secret process)
metals.magical_properties: Adds +2 bonus to saving throws of awakening, enchant an item, holy vesting, and wondrous web spells cast on it. Auto-succeeds vs. normal fire, cold, and electricity. +4 vs. acid, crushing blow, disintegration, fall, magical fire, and lightning.
metals.notes: Black with clear green sheen in candlelight; sharpens to purple-white under magical radiances and will-o-wisps. Must be worked at very high temperatures by expert dwarven smiths. Best nonmithral armor material.

metals.name: Arandur
metals.magical_properties: Bonds with other metals so well that Merald's Meld and crown meld are unnecessary when enchanting items made of it with other metals. Famous for holding an exceptionally sharp edge even under abuse. Partially absorbs magic missile energy: bearer takes 1d2 fewer points per bolt (minimum 1). Auto-succeeds vs. fall, normal fire, cold, electricity. +3 vs. acid, crushing blow, disintegration, magical fire, lightning.
metals.notes: Silver-blue with green reflective shine. Found in igneous rock as streaks in vitreous glass; must be tempered with red or blue dragon blood in forging. Once exclusive to gnomes; now also worked by elven smiths of Evereska and Evermeet. Favored for swords of sharpness and vorpal weapons.

metals.name: Copper
metals.magical_properties: Best widely available purifier and amalgamator. An item not suited to a wizard's or priest's faith or purpose can be made usable by adding at least half the item's weight in copper. Holy or unholy water stored in copper vessels for 2d4 months is neutralized to plain water. Items primarily of copper save at normal metal listings.
metals.notes: No magical bonuses to saving throws beyond the standard metal tables.

metals.name: Darksteel
metals.magical_properties: Absorbs all natural and magical lightning or electrical energy (not heat or magic missiles) without conducting any of it to the wearer. Remarkably, can be melted and recast without destroying or usually altering existing enchantments on it. Takes new enchantments readily even when already dweomer-laden. Auto-succeeds vs. fall, normal fire, cold, electricity. +3 vs. acid, crushing blow, disintegration, magical fire. +5 vs. lightning.
metals.notes: Silvery when polished or cut, but with a deep gleaming purple luster on exposed surfaces. Possibly extinct Ironstar dwarven clan's secret; only old ingots remain. Valued at 10–12x gold by weight; Neverwinter and Waterdeep smiths offer 7,000+ gp for an intact ingot.

metals.name: Dlarun
metals.magical_properties: Steadies the mind of any being in direct bare-flesh contact with it: +1 bonus to all saves vs. enchantment/charm and illusion/phantasm spells and similar psionic or spell-like effects. Auto-succeeds vs. fall, normal fire, cold, electricity (treated as arandur in the text for saving throws). +1 vs. acid, crushing blow, disintegration, magical fire, lightning.
metals.notes: Bone-white; often mistaken for ivory; distinctive greenish sheen in candlelight and near magical radiances. Derived from clay dug from certain riverbanks by a complex halfling process; kept as close a secret as possible.

metals.name: Gold
metals.magical_properties: Holds multiple conflicting enchantments without destabilizing each other or the item. Makes all dweomerflow magics entering an item containing even very small amounts of gold automatically succeed (no saving throw needed for magical charge transfers at the receiving end). Items primarily of gold save at normal metal listings.
metals.notes: No bonus to item saving throws.

metals.name: Hizagkuur
metals.magical_properties: Reflects all magic cast at it 100% back at its source. Deals 2d12 electrical damage per touch (or per round of continued contact) to all beings touching it. Auto-succeeds vs. normal fire, cold, electricity. +6 vs. magical fire and lightning. +1 vs. acid, crushing blow, fall, disintegration.
metals.notes: Cannot be used in magical items or worn items — immediately injurious. Named for its dwarven discoverer. Found only as soft clay or flaky mud deep in the Underdark. Must be cast into its final form within one day of preparation or it becomes permanently inert. Used only as sheathing for fortress gates, vault doors, and sealed hatches.

metals.name: Mithral
metals.magical_properties: Against magical attacks: roll 1d12 each time magic contacts it. Odd: nothing. Even: either +1 bonus to saving throws for nearby beings (the wearer) or –1 point per die of magical damage (whichever is more favorable to the mithral wearer). Lightest metal hard enough for armor. Auto-succeeds vs. normal fire, cold, electricity. +2 vs. acid, disintegration, magical fire, lightning. +6 vs. crushing blow and fall.
metals.notes: Silvery-blue and shining. Can be combined with steel to derive adamantine. Extremely valuable. Can be combined with silver in dwarven alloy processes to create lightning-warding alloys.

metals.name: Silver
metals.magical_properties: The most magical of all metals. If silver is the dominant ingredient (60%+) of an item and the item involves moon-related magics, electricity or lightning, or pure energy discharges (magic missiles): all saving throws for awakening, enchant an item, holy vesting, wondrous web, Merald's meld, crown meld, Obar's lesser purification, Azundel's purification, higher consecration, and other purification spells automatically succeed. At 50–60% silver: +4 bonus to all such saves. For all other item types: 50%+ silver content gives +2 bonus to rolls for purification, strengthening, and melding spell success. Items primarily of silver save at normal metal listings.
metals.notes: "The sheath and shield of Art." Certain elven folk and senior Harpers know additional secret silver processes.

metals.name: Telstang
metals.magical_properties: The wearer and all organic material in contact with or encased in it cannot be affected by paralyzation, polymorph, disintegrate, petrification, shape change, or similar attacks. However, also cannot benefit from beneficial magical state changes (spider climb, water breathing, etc.). Auto-succeeds vs. normal fire, cold, electricity. +2 vs. acid, disintegration, magical fire, lightning. Saves normally vs. crushing blow and fall.
metals.notes: Dull silver in hue; a "singing metal" (clear bell tone when struck). Never oxidizes; lasts forever if not struck or dropped. Too brittle for weapons or armor; worn as bracers, buckles, brooches, pendants. Originally a gnomish secret; adopted by halflings and certain elven and orc peoples.

metals.name: Zardazil
metals.magical_properties: When a zardazil weapon wounds its first creature (sometimes done deliberately): after 1 full turn, the weapon permanently body-phases with that being and can never harm them again; instead it passes harmlessly through their body. The weapon can be carried concealed inside the body (attached to a nonmetal anchor to prevent falling through). Out of reach of all spells targeting it through the body. Does not affect bodily processes, weight, or spells on the person.
metals.notes: Very soft; never used in pure form — alloyed or used as sheathing only. Found only around the Lake of Steam and in Raurin sand fissures. Blade does not pass through clothing harmlessly; sheath can also body-phase if all-metal with zardazil. Multiple anchors can prevent unintended weapon exposure.

metals.name: Adarcer
metals.description: White alloy of ang (iron), glôin ("True-coal"), and durang (titanium). Extremely strong but rigid and difficult to work once forged. Can cleave iron without dulling.

metals.name: Alcam
metals.description: Soft, silvery metal normally used to make evyth (bronze). Dwarves use it to line water-basins and for decorative filigree. Elves employ it as building facings, roofing, and combine it with paer to make bronze.

metals.name: Ang
metals.description: Pure ang is silver-white, malleable, and ductile — rare even in Moria. The more common variety is dark grey and harder. Found throughout the mines of the northern Deeps.

metals.name: Arborang
metals.description: Alloy (iron/carbon/varies); high steel.

metals.name: Arheled
metals.description: Listed in the properties chart; description not given in the prose sections.

metals.name: Borang
metals.description: Alloy of ang, morasarn (carbon), and trace metals. Strong and durable; cheaper and more pliable than adarcer. The Mírdain consider it unattractive but use it extensively.

metals.name: Celeb
metals.description: Used for decorative inlays, chalices, plates, and cups. Despite its malleability, stronger than mal (gold). Prized and used extensively by the Noldor.

metals.name: Celebur
metals.description: Weak uranium-like ore. Known to Dwarves, who avoid it. Required for the making of mithrarian.

metals.name: Cranor
metals.description: Golden translucent resin, invented by the ancient Daen folk of the White Mountains. Made from Sorglasora sap and White Lily nectar. Nearly as hard as a diamond and highly resistant to fracture. Stores static electricity up to 1,000 volts, released as a Lightning Bolt-equivalent attack when an ungrounded object touches it. Used to entomb Dunnish chieftains.

metals.name: Eog
metals.description: Fusion of mithril, durang (titanium), and unknown materials from an Elven recipe of the House of Eöl. Requires both the hottest and coldest forges of Khazad-dûm. Harder than adarcer, stronger than ithilnaur. Dampens Essence manipulation within a radius depending on the spellcaster. Comes in white, red, black, blue, and grey.

metals.name: Evyth
metals.description: Alloy of alcam and paer. Used by Dwarves for decoration; traded to Men of Rhovanion as a cheap ang substitute. Favorite common metal of the Elves for building, sculpture, and decoration.
metals.notes: ~90,000 gp/oz per chart (likely OCR error); Bonus: –10

metals.name: Galnin
metals.description: Silvery-white, light, and non-tarnishing/non-corroding. Extremely rare. Dwarves consider it insubstantial; most of what they mine goes to the Noldor. Used as an undercoat for mithrarian application at Amon Lind.

metals.name: Galvorn
metals.description: Rarest metal in Middle-earth; first developed by Eöl. Malleable yet cut/puncture-resistant; the hardest substance when specially forged. Made partly from meteoric iron. Only Celebrimbor and Fendomë among the Eregion smiths might have rediscovered the process.

metals.name: Heled
metals.description: Glass, listed in the properties chart.

metals.name: Ithildin
metals.description: Soft, silvery Elven metal invented by Celebrimbor, fused from mithril and other substances. Appears dull by day; glows silvery-white under moonlight and starlight. Used almost exclusively for secret inscriptions and magical purposes. May be the medium for Dwarvish Moon-letters.

metals.name: Ithilnaur
metals.description: Mithril alloyed with titanium and other metals, folded and hammered dozens of times to create an extremely strong laminate. Hard, maintains a keen edge, and somewhat flexible. Surprisingly common in Moria; rarer elsewhere. Resembles pure silver in appearance.

metals.name: Kregora
metals.description: Extremely ductile; too malleable for weapons or jewelry, and oxidizes to a dull yellow patina. Its utility lies in blocking Mentalism, Channeling, and Essence spells from passing through surfaces lined with wire, threads, or netting of the substance.

metals.name: Laen
metals.description: Volcanic glass. Gains rigidity with heat; must be chilled to sculpt. Natural color black or smoky; can be cleared or tinted. Treated further in Section 6.4 (Stones / Mirond).

metals.name: Mal
metals.description: Soft, non-tarnishing; does not corrode. Dwarves value it above all metals save mithril. Elves prize it as a beautiful metal and use it in strong alloys unknown to Dwarves. Mixed with mithglín to make white-gold.

metals.name: Mithglín
