metals.description: Rare, shining hue; difficult to forge, requiring high temperatures and hard labor. Resulting jewelry is more durable than gold or silver work. Often combined with mal to form workable white-gold.

metals.name: Mithin
metals.description: Rare, strong, light material used mostly in jewelry. Few smiths, even among the Elves, know how to work it. Dwarves delight in creating seemingly fragile baubles from it.

metals.name: Mithrarian
metals.description: Legendary alloy of mithril, eog, and celebur, introduced by Annatar (Sauron in disguise) to the Gwaith-i-Mírdain. Objects coated in mithrarian float without weight, and the material resists all counter-spells. Never made in any reputable smithy; only perfected at Amon Lind in the Misty Mountains.

metals.name: Mithril
metals.description: Shining white and malleable like silver, but never tarnishes and alloys to produce enchanted metals of incomparable quality. Always appears polished. The single known vein runs from the Seventh Deep of Moria under Barazinbar. Dwarves dug so deeply for it that they released the Balrog; no mithril came from Moria after T.A. 1980. Valued above all other metals by Dwarves and treasured by Elves and Dúnedain alike.

metals.name: Ogamur
metals.description: Extremely flexible and elastic black metal, ideal for springs and impact-absorbing devices. Derived from an Eastern Dwarf-house recipe withheld from the Noldor, who must purchase it from Durin's folk.

metals.name: Paer
metals.description: Reddish-gold; common and low in value. Used by Dwarves for water-troughs, basins, and evyth production. Men use it for pots, pans, gutters, statues, and roofing. The Noldor regard it more highly and use it for building and pipe-work.

metals.name: Tasarang
metals.description: Bends easily with tremendous spring, but does not stretch. Extremely light — even lighter than galnin. White chalk-like ore found below limestone. More than one metalworker claims it glows. Used to make powerful bows; the material's rarity makes this impractical in most situations.

treatments.name: Blueshine
treatments.source_material: Dwarven process; duplicated by the wizard Toth's 4th-level Alteration spell (Wiz 4; V, S, M; Touch; Permanent; Cast 4)
treatments.effect: Purges all oxidation; prevents future rusting; purges fractures and blemishes; treated metals glow with a deep blue sheen in available light. +1 bonus to all item saves vs. acid and all corrosive effects (venom, various bloods, ochre jelly secretions, black dragon acid).
treatments.notes: Toth was slain by Red Wizards for developing the spell; the spell was already stolen by a rival before their attempt to suppress it. Spell material component: a small piece of cobalt blue glass or a chip of a blue-hued gemstone.

treatments.name: Everbright
treatments.source_material: Dwarven process; no spell equivalent discovered yet
treatments.effect: Grants an enduring bright shine (like chromium); immune to tarnishing, discoloration, acidic corrosion, and rusting — including rust monster antenna attacks. Protection does not fade with time.
treatments.notes: Can be broken if: item is shattered into more than three pieces, or comes into contact with lava, dragon fire, spellfire, or forge heat exceeding that of the everbright process itself. At least three mages and one archpriest have conducted long-running research to create a spell equivalent, all without success.

treatments.name: Halabar's Stealth
treatments.source_material: Process devised by the House of Halabar merchant clan, Murann
treatments.effect: Renders metallic items nonferromagnetic, nonreflective, and silent (no clanging even when struck against other metals or stone). Items can take dyes and paints (even bare sword blades).
treatments.notes: Formula known only to Halabar's descendants, who guard it viciously. Still strikes sparks at sharp impact and conducts lightning normally. Secret formula; rumored intelligent shapechanger agents defend it against lore thieves.

treatments.name: Everbright
treatments.source_material: Dwarven metallurgical process; a wizard spell (Wiz 4, Alteration) duplicating its effects was developed by Toth of Calimport and published here for the first time (the wizard was killed by Red Wizards attempting to suppress it, but the spell had already been stolen by a rival and survived).
treatments.effect: Purges all existing oxidation from metals and prevents future rusting. Purges fractures and blemishes from the item, leaving it whole and appearing like new. All treated metals glow with a deep blue sheen when they catch available light. Grants +1 bonus to all item saving throws vs. acid and all corrosive effects — venom, various creature bloods, ochre jelly secretions, black dragon acid. | Level 4 / Casting time 4 / Components V, S, M / Range touch / Area the metal parts of one item not exceeding the caster's body volume / Duration permanent / Saving throw none.

treatments.source_material: Dwarven metallurgical process. No spell equivalent has been found despite long-running research by at least three mages (Athlagh of the Many Locks, Halandrar Crowncloak, and Spelargh of Phelzol) and one archpriest (Beltorvan Duircragh, Bright Blade of Tempus in the Bloodbright Temple of Dolselar).

stones.name: Dirielong
stones.description: Broad Dwarvish category for softer metamorphic and sedimentary stones used decoratively or where Naurond is unwieldy. Sub-types: "Block-stones" (colored marble and softer "Wet-rocks"/limestone), and "Slab-stones" (schist, flint, slate). Limestone cave formations — stalactites and stalagmites — are called "Aulë's Tears" by Dwarves and preserved wherever possible during delving.

stones.name: Naurond
stones.description: General Dwarvish term for volcanic/igneous rock; the stone that binds Moria. Coarse granite near the surface; smooth black basalt deeper in. A light pumice variety from the "Domes" of the Fifth Deep is used as a polishing/grinding material; rarely sold to non-Dwarves.

stones.name: Mirond
stones.description: Dwarvish classification system for gems and glasses. Two principal categories: Fenen ("Veils" / "Hidden Crystals" / "Glasses") and Maegelenath ("Sharp-stars" / "Bold Crystals" / "Gemstones"). Of the glasses, laen is the most intriguing — as hard as diamond, smooth, without cleavage points, and colorable when worked.
stones.notes: Quartzes and obsidians provide most of Moria's glasses; no single Dwarven gemstone is considered preeminent.

stones.name: Ulgond
stones.description: Elven liquid stone poured into wood molds; hardens after a few days to a hardness exceeding any natural rock. Used extensively by the Gwaith-i-Mírdain.

woods.name: Beetle Palm
woods.item_properties: Wood conveys no special properties to items.
woods.component_properties: Nuts used as substitute components in the goodberry priest spell: nourish creatures up to Huge size or heal 1d2+2 damage; no daily maximum; nuts remain magical and do not rot for one year.
woods.notes: Oily, very flammable; burns nearly 3x as long as other wood with half the smoke. Nuts are black, bitter, plum-sized. Casting badberry on beetle palm nuts does not work — the whole batch simply goes bad instead.

woods.name: Blueleaf
woods.location: North of Amn to Impiltur; rare specimens in Chessenta, Turmish, Border Kingdoms
woods.item_properties: Durable, neutral wood — neither aids nor hampers enchantment.
woods.component_properties: If the sole consumed component in a spell (not counting a holy symbol or item being altered), reduces casting time by 1, to a minimum of 1.
woods.notes: Electric blue leaves; yielding blue dye. Yields leaping blue flames when burned.

woods.name: Calantra
woods.location: Forest of Tethir; north Chult to Shaar
woods.item_properties: All item saving throws at +2 bonus over other woods. Increases to +3 bonus if the item is at least 20% calantra and bears any enchantment (not cumulative beyond +3).
woods.component_properties: No special properties; can be used safely wherever any nonspecific wood product is called for.
woods.notes: Heartwood of the calan tree; red-barked, low, gnarly crown. Exceptionally durable; resists frost, fire (even dragon breath), and floods.

woods.name: Chime Oak
woods.item_properties: Items primarily of chime oak: auto-succeed at all item saves vs. cold. Items with less than 45% chime oak retain a +1 bonus vs. cold.
woods.component_properties: Can substitute for normal oak interchangeably in spells but otherwise has no special component properties.
woods.notes: Resembles a glass oak; leaves freeze solid in autumn and tinkle like wind chimes — attractive to basilisks. Wood becomes silvery-white when dry. Sweet, pure sound in magical musical instruments.

woods.name: Duskwood
woods.item_properties: Suitable for staves and rods. Severely hinders item enchantment: caster of every eternal flame involved must save vs. spell at –2 or the spell fails, destroying prior enchantments on the item. Exception: augments fire-resistance items and spells by +1 point per die of fiery damage warded.
woods.component_properties: In fire-related spell components: adds 20% chance of total spell failure (applied after casting; all other components consumed, duskwood remains). Exception for fire-resistance spells: augments protection by 1 point per die.
woods.notes: Hardest wood in common use; most mast spars and roof beams in Faerûn. Smolders rather than blazes; survives forest fires.

woods.name: Felsul
woods.component_properties: Universal replacement component for spells hastening withering, decay, or increasing damage — one chip of felsul (wood, bark, or root) suffices per spell, replacing normal components (if not specially constructed).
woods.notes: Gnarled, twisted, crumbling bark; grows on crags and cliff edges. Felsul root prized for carving small holy symbols and figurines. Yellow-and-purple flowers in early spring yield perfume worth up to 3 gp per sack in scarce years.

woods.name: Hiexel
woods.location: Common in the Dales (ravines and hillsides)
woods.item_properties: Unsuitable for magical items: unstable nature causes any such item to break after 1d2 years of service at most.
woods.component_properties: Cannot be used as a component for any magic involving water or liquids. Universal replacement for spells involving mists or vapors: increases casting time by 1, no other effect.
woods.notes: Brittle, green, waxy wood; rots easily; produces thick oily smoke when ignited. Bark is silver-green, resistant to burning and rot; used as book binding and building facing in damp locations.

woods.name: Laspar
woods.location: Everywhere north of mid-Tethyr and west of Thay
woods.item_properties: Unsuitable for magical items and all permanent magic.
woods.component_properties: Universal replacement component for spells involving transformations of shape or state: decreases casting time by 1.
woods.notes: Squat cedar-like evergreen; pitchy wood that spits many sparks, unsafe for burning. Boiled needles are an effective laxative; crushed needles used in quality torch and candle scents.

woods.name: Phandar
woods.location: Rare; seldom north of mid-High Forest; heavily cut
woods.item_properties: Ideal for durable magical items that need not be straight. Essential ingredient in all healing potions and enchanted unguents. Prolongs all wondrous web or holy vesting spells cast on items at least partially of phandar wood by one additional round. Requires no purification magics.
woods.notes: Greenish-brown wood with curving grain; makes striking wave patterns when cut. Hardy — thrives even from waste boughs; stumps regrow; practically extinction-proof despite heavy cutting.

woods.name: Roseneedle Pine
woods.component_properties: Tinctures from tubers or flowers: used in preparation of items controlling or summoning aquatic life. Needles: universal replacement for any sort of fish or fish part required as a material component in a spell.
woods.notes: Miniature evergreen (max 3 ft tall). Roots spread 10+ ft with fat potato-sized tubers. Tubers also double as exceptional fishing bait, doubling a day's catch.

woods.name: Shadowtop
woods.location: Widespread except arctic; most common large magical wood
woods.item_properties: Much used in staves, rods, and wands. Crown melds never necessary when item contains shadow wood — Merald's meld joins on shadow wood automatically succeed at their saving throws and die rolls (treat as having a crown meld). Always considered properly harvested and bathed for whatever enchantment it will receive, regardless of actual procurement.
woods.notes: Soaring giants of Faerûn's forests; 90+ ft tall; 20+ ft diameter at base; feathery dense leaf crown. Wood is fibrous and tough; splits under structural stress. Burns slowly, cleanly, and very hot with little smoke.

woods.name: Silverbark
woods.location: Wet ground, bogs, and swamps throughout Faerûn
woods.item_properties: Unsuitable for lance shafts, structural work, or most long-term items.
woods.component_properties: Universal replacement component in all purification and antitoxin magics: reduces casting time by 1 and replaces all other normally required components (unless specially constructed).
woods.notes: Thin, straight; max 15 ft tall, 4 inches diameter. Reddish wood; very brittle once dry. Sap: essential in poison antidotes and sweet water potions.

woods.name: Suth
woods.location: Shaar edges, Chondath, and farther south
woods.item_properties: Items primarily of suth wood: +2 bonus to item saves vs. crushing blow and fall.
woods.component_properties: Suth wood slivers or bark chips: can replace all components (if not specially constructed) for barkskin, armor, and similar toughening spells, and for Veladar's Vambrace and holy might. Suth sap: essential ingredient in the oil used to anoint metal armor and shields before enchanting them to improve their AC.
woods.notes: Tangled, nearly horizontal growth; interlocking stands form impassable walls. Hard enough to require the finest tools. Preferred shield wood (never shatters; fire-resistant if pre-soaked).

woods.name: Vundwood
woods.location: Tunland; south of Iriaebor into Western Heartlands and Green Fields
woods.item_properties: Echo property: items made of vundwood spontaneously gain 1d4 charges from nowhere once every 1d12 months, unless the item is totally exhausted of charges.
woods.component_properties: Universal replacement for all consumed components in any priest or wizard spell involving recalling an already-cast spell or augmenting/altering the caster's spell capacity (e.g., Rary's mnemonic enhancer).
woods.notes: Short, scrubby; max 15 ft; no central trunk; many radiating branches. Reddish-brown wood with a cinnamon smell.

woods.name: Weirwood
woods.location: Rare; deep forests of Faerûn; protected by dryads, treants, druids, and rangers
woods.item_properties: Does not burn in normal fire. Any magically generated radiance (dancing lights, etc.) brought into contact with cut or living weirwood lingers around it for 1d4+1 rounds after the source expires or is removed — unless the weirwood bears any active enchantment on itself (which negates this property).
woods.component_properties: Replaces all spells normally requiring oak or holly (bark, leaves, berries, or wood). Can replace any one non-specially-constructed consumed component in spells creating magical radiance or providing protection or resistance to fire. Used as an extra component in creation/mending spells (mending, wondrous web, awakening, enchant an item, holy vesting, ritual of transference): +1 bonus to all saves and ability checks in the spellcasting.
woods.notes: Resembles an oak but with brown leaves having a silver upper sheen and velvety black undersides. Warm, clear sound in musical instruments.

woods.name: Zalantar
woods.location: Subtropical; common along Chult's shores and southern Faerûn coasts
woods.item_properties: +2 bonus to saving throws for priest or wizard awakening and wizard enchant an item spells. +1 bonus to all item saving throws for any enchanted or nonenchanted item wholly or partially of zalantar while in use. Glows faint mauve when undead beings are within a 70-ft spherical radius.
woods.notes: Black wood; white-to-beige leaves. Grows from a single root with 8+ trunks splaying like fingers. Up to 80 ft tall, average 40 ft. Strong, easily worked; used in southern buildings, wagons, litters, wheels. Southern sorcerers use it almost exclusively for rods, staves, and wands.

woods.name: Black Cypress
woods.description: Up to 200' tall; dark trunk, scale-like leaves. Grows throughout the Western Dominions of the Metharn. Produces some of the finest ship-building lumber in Middle-earth. Hard to work, but finished items are exceptionally strong (equivalent to –5 iron).

woods.name: Blue Pine
woods.description: Most common evergreen of the Rhudaur; bluish-silver wood. High tannic-acid content acts as a natural preservative — structures last twice as long as those of other woods. Large cones carry edible seeds (pine nuts).
woods.notes: Also listed under Herbs (Section 6.2) for its edible seeds.

woods.name: Chap-beech
woods.description: Bark gleams unearthly white (especially under the new moon); leaves hiss in the wind. Seed pods are stinging and venomous on bare skin — immobilize the victim. "Walls" of Chap-beech guard the path to Dol Guldur. Only Beijabar raccoons (leather-pawed and immune to the venom) harvest the nuts safely; the roasted kernels are nutritious and pleasant.
woods.notes: Twenty-five roasted kernels make a meal.

woods.name: Dírwood
woods.description: Darkest black conifer of the extreme northern latitudes. When properly cured, as hard as the toughest steel and holds an edge as well or better. A different curing process yields a springy laminate for bows with exceptional range. Focuses the Essence while growing; particularly suited to Alchemical use.

woods.name: Furry Oak
woods.description: Related to White Oak; round-lobed deep-red leaves with a quarter-inch of fuzz on the underside. Grows very large acorns (big as plums); all fall on the same day each autumn. Edible raw or baked; stores indefinitely if kept dry.
woods.notes: Squirrels and Woodman-wives scramble to gather the harvest; Elves of Lórien frequently cross the river for them.

woods.name: Goldwood
woods.description: Reaches 300' in height and 60' in girth; ancient, rare, and exceedingly tough. Used by the Fuinar of Valagalen as homesites — Elves carve rooms inside the living trunk without endangering it. Grows southwest of Endor around the Bay of Drel.

woods.name: Grape-leaf Magnolia
woods.description: Most abundant broad-leaf evergreen in Mirkwood. Blood-red flowers in July. Honey made from the nectar is dark red, sweet, nutritious, and intoxicating in excess. Beijabar make Magnolia Mead from it; drunk only at solemn or festive feasts.
woods.notes: Groves are unapproachable in peak bloom due to swarming bees.

woods.name: Greddon
woods.description: One of three tree types in the Gaj ("The Grove") of Far Harad; valued for its strong, sinuous wood.

woods.name: Gumumiti
woods.description: Tall tropical hardwood, 120' in common growth; resinous yellow-brown wood. Found throughout Tathorn, Taur Galen, and Thunderwood, and in smaller form in the Yellow Mountains and Valagalen. Used for rich inlays, furniture, saddles, and shields. Requires frequent reoiling or it cracks.
woods.notes: Leaves also medicinal (see Herbs: Lainimit leaves / Welwal).

woods.name: Juha
woods.description: Great tower of the southern forests; mast timber for the tallest ships of Umbar. Grows for years as a tiny shoot; lowest branches are ~100' up by the time the trunk is climbable. Harvested for spars and later for masts.
woods.notes: Source of the lethal Karfar poison from its leaves (see Herbs).

woods.name: Lainimit
woods.description: Reddish-brown or tan; hard, beautiful, and highly useful. Common and tall (up to 90'). Major source of revenue in the Eastern Dominions. Also produces the medicinal Welwal leaves (see Herbs).

woods.name: Lebethron
woods.description: Dark hardwood; common in Gondor and the Ered Nimrais. Renowned for beauty and durability; used for masts of Gondor's finest vessels. (A Lebethron box houses the Silver Crown of the realm.) High Knights wield Lebethron lances; Gondorian Rangers carry Lebethron staffs. Faramir gave Sam and Frodo walking staves of this wood.

woods.name: Mallorn
woods.description: Hardy, strong, able to grow to great heights, with branches suited to the platforms and structures of the Silvan Elves. Trunks covered in smooth silver-white or grey bark. Leaves turn pure gold in late autumn and remain until spring, when pale gold blossoms emerge. Do not die of old age; immune to all disease and plague. Not native to Middle-earth — originated in the Undying Lands; likely related to Laurelin of the Two Trees. Brought to Lórien via Galadriel with seeds gifted by Gil-galad (received from the Númenórean King Tar-Aldarion). The second Party Tree in the Shire was a mallorn — the only one in Eriador.

woods.name: Oiolairé
woods.description: Glossy, sweet-scented evergreen; once grew around Fornost Erain. Destroyed forever when Angmar's invaders burned the lands of Arthedain.

woods.name: Shadamabo
woods.description: Heavy, hard, reddish tropical hardwood; up to 100' tall. Used for sturdy furniture and durable spears.

woods.name: Slird
woods.description: Short citrus tree; fine orange-yellow wood with a permanent fresh scent. Used for chests and wardrobes to keep clothes smelling pleasant and to discourage moths.
woods.notes: Bright red fruit is poisonous (see Herbs).

woods.name: Sorglasora
woods.description: Rare red-leaved conifer, now found only in isolated mountain valleys in Lebennin, hidden among common pines. Principal ingredient in Cranor manufacture. Prized by the Dunnish people but nearly cut to extinction by their over-harvesting.

woods.name: Tordi
woods.description: Common among the Gaj of Far Harad; up to 80' tall with broad, faintly reddish leaves spreading more horizontally than vertically. Strong and flexible when steamed; holds its shape. Used for ship ribs and other applications requiring both strength and give.

woods.name: Usamiti
woods.description: Hard, dense, often jet black; as prized as jade or gold. Tropical and rare even in the Eastern Dominions where it is most commonly found.

woods.name: Yellow Hemlock
woods.description: Graceful pyramidal evergreen, up to 75'. Fairly soft for an evergreen; useful for carvings, amulets, grills, necklace beads, and other decorative purposes. Layers can be laminated for larger sculptures and totems.
woods.notes: Resin is a powerful coagulant (see Herbs).

enchanted.name: Dragon Horn
enchanted.description: Essentially unbreakable. Size and rib pattern signals a drake's power and denotes its stature in the species hierarchy. Prized for musical instruments and bow-making; can be ground to produce a host of enchanted potions.

enchanted.name: Dragonskin
enchanted.description: Highly valued as armor material; strength varies with the dragon's age (overlapping plates grow thicker over time). To harvest, an adventurer must contend with the dragon's toxic blood while cutting the scales and underlying hide. Making usable armor requires both an armourer and an alchemist.

enchanted.name: Dragon Blood
enchanted.description: Caustic and enchanted; difficult to store, transport, and utilize due to its corrosive properties. Can be made into potions granting the imbiber temporary ability to use mind-manipulating spells. Grows more powerful and more dangerously acidic as the dragon ages.

spells.name: Dweomerflow
spells.range: 20 yards or touch / — / One person or one item
spells.effect: Two casting modes. **Mode 1 (spell redirect):** Cast on a spellcaster (self or another); the recipient's next spell flows into a prepared receptacle — a focal stone, crystal ball, magical item needing recharging, or similar vessel — instead of taking its normal effect. No saving throws apply. If no valid receptacle is in range when the spell takes effect, a ghostly radiance appears and fades within the round; the spell is wasted. **Mode 2 (charge transfer):** Transfers charges or stored spells from one item to another. The caster must touch both items to bridge the energy. Both items save vs. spell: if the sending item fails, the spell is ruined but nothing is lost; if the receiving item fails, the transferred charge or spell is lost — sometimes spectacularly.

spells.name: Merald's Meld
spells.effect: Permanently binds two objects together without physical fasteners. The caster touches both items and positions them in the desired join; the magic fuses them unbreakably under normal circumstances. Living or undead material cannot be melded. The two items are not altered — a given item can be involved in any number of melds. The join can be broken by four *dispel magic* spells targeted specifically at it, unless a *crown meld* was later applied, in which case the item is entirely impervious to dispel magic. If the item fails an item saving throw, a meld is more likely to fail (separating the pieces cleanly) than the materials themselves are to be damaged — unless a crown meld was applied, in which case joins never separate this way. *Material components:* a flake or drop of resin, an iron filing, a strand of spider silk, and a paste of ground legumes.

spells.name: Obar's Lesser Purification
spells.range: 3 yards / One item or volume of liquid or raw materials no greater than the caster's body volume / —
spells.effect: Destroys curses, magical tracers, and remnants of previous magics on a single nonliving item or body of liquid. Causes the target to glow to reveal active or dormant dweomers, but does not trigger, identify, or alter them. Also works on dry or powdered materials gathered into a continuous volume. Does not affect recently living materials (dead less than a month, or undead). Secondary function: purges liquids — potions, tinctures, unguents — of natural or magical impurities simultaneously with the main dweomer-purging. *Material components:* a pinch of limestone dust, a pinch of salt, and three drops of a *potion of sweet water.* ### 5th Level

spells.name: Abeyance
spells.range: Touch / — / 1 focal stone or 1 magical item
spells.effect: Two modes. **Mode 1 (freeze a focal stone):** Freezes a spell already cast into a focal stone, holding it in suspension indefinitely. The abeyance is broken by a *dweomerflow*, *wondrous web*, or *holy vesting* spell (which conveys the stored magic onward without releasing it), by shattering the focal stone (which releases the spell instantly), or by certain other extraction spells. *Dispel magic* is specifically not one of these. **Mode 2 (delay an item activation):** The caster touches a magical item (not an artifact) with bare flesh at casting; the next time that item is activated, its effect is delayed 1 round. The abeyance then dissipates.

spells.name: Eternal Flame
spells.range: Touch / One item or body not exceeding twice the caster's own body volume / —
spells.effect: Two targets. **On an item:** Imbues the item with a receptive neutral enchantment so that later spells cast at it (or transferred into it via *dweomerflow*) enter it without a saving throw, transfer failure, or damage — up to one spell or effect per level of the *eternal flame* caster. Does not make the item usable; only allows it to hold magics. The window for imbuing powers closes when an *awakening* spell is cast. If the item is shattered before awakening, stored magics release explosively. **On a mammalian body (living, dead, or undead):** The next spell to contact the prepared body takes full effect at maximum potency with no saving throw, system shock, or resurrection survival roll required. Exceptions: enchantment/charm and illusion/phantasm spells are not affected by eternal flame. *Material component:* a spark struck by a dweomer-bearing item against a rock, bladed weapon, or dweomer-bearing metal item; neither item is harmed.

spells.name: Focal Stone
spells.range: Touch / — / 1 clear or translucent crystalline gemstone no larger than the caster's balled fist
spells.save: Special (item save vs. magical fire at casting; failure destroys the gem)
spells.effect: Restructures a clear or translucent crystalline gemstone to hold a spell dweomer. On success the stone glows with a soft internal radiance and emits a faint dweomer. Exceptional-quality stones may receive a +1 to +3 bonus to the saving throw. Special property: if immersed in a poisonous liquid the focal stone turns vivid purple; it can then be commanded by touch and will to neutralize the poison, after which it dissolves and is destroyed. Common misconceptions aside, a focal stone cannot trap passing spells or draw in enchanted creatures. It resists natural and magical heat, flame, lava, extreme cold, and mineral contamination, but not deliberate crushing. Shattering it releases any stored spell instantly in a manner the DM determines. *Dispel magic* has no effect on a focal stone or its contents. *Material component:* a pinch of opal dust of any type.

spells.name: Veladar's Vambrace
spells.range: Touch / One item no larger in volume than the caster's body volume / —
spells.effect: Strengthens inorganic substances so they do not rot or age. The item may contain organic substances (glues, etc.) only if they are less than one-tenth of total volume; otherwise the spell fails. Existing fractures and blemishes are purged; the item appears like new. Fragile substances are hardened, and hard substances made more resilient; the item gains +5 on all saving throws vs. acid, crushing blow, disintegration, fall, normal fire, and cold. *Material components:* a whole diamond of not less than 2,000 gp value; a sliver or chunk of ironwood of the same size or larger than the diamond; a piece of chitin of about the same size from a beholder, ankheg, or bulette; and a drop of giant slug spittle. ### 6th Level

spells.name: Crown Meld
spells.effect: Required when more than four different substances are used in a magical item's construction, or when four or more *Merald's meld* spells are applied. Weaves multiple preexisting melds into a resilient whole, treating all joined pieces as one unflawed continuous object. When the item must make a saving throw, it uses the most favorable saving throw of any of its component substances for each situation (e.g., a wood-and-glass scepter saves as thin wood vs. a fall but as glass vs. fire). A crown-melded item is entirely impervious to dispel magic targeting its joins and never separates at a meld due to a failed item saving throw. *Material components:* a lump of resin as large as the caster's thumb, an iron nail, a strand of spider silk, a handful of paste of ground legumes, and a flawless diamond of any size and at least 2,000 gp value.

spells.name: Wondrous Web
spells.effect: Transfers magical powers from source items into a destination item at one power or control property per round. Sources may be potions, spell scrolls, parchments inscribed with magical command words, focal stones, or existing magical items. The transfer creates a visible humming network of glowing white lines of force between all items involved. Powers are held in the destination item in stable magical stasis until an *awakening* spell is cast. Only existing magical items get a saving throw: base 7 for items with fewer than three functions; base 9 plus one per function beyond four for items with four or more functions. A successful save means no effect; failure means a random function is drawn out. Charge-based functions lose 1d4 charges per round rather than the function itself; non-charge functions are permanently stripped. If ended prematurely by the caster's will or by *dispel magic*, magic in transit is lost; already-transferred powers and untouched sources are unaffected. Missiles striking a *wondrous web* are teleported 1d6×10 feet in a random direction but are otherwise unharmed. *Material components:* six strands of spider silk and a piece of fishing net or lace. ### 7th Level

spells.name: Awakening
spells.effect: Activates a multi-enchantment item. Requires *eternal flame* and usually *wondrous web* (or *holy vesting*) and *dweomerflow* castings first. Can also be used to add new powers to an existing *enchant an item* item once all original powers have been used at least once. The item makes a saving throw using the caster's save vs. spell, modified: –1 per being other than the caster who contributed magic; +1 per *Merald's meld* and *crown meld* existing on the item; +1 if both *eternal flame* and *Veladar's vambrace*, *Nulathoe's ninemen*, or *holy might* were cast on the item. A natural 1 always fails. Failure: roll 1d6 — 1 or 2, explosion as a fireball (1d6 damage per caster level) and item destroyed; 4–6, item collapses to magically inert dust carried away by a sudden wind. Success: item activates instantly; a flash of light may occur but is never a harmful discharge. *Material components:* a wizard spell scroll bearing at least as many spells as the item has functions; a gem of any kind worth at least 2,500 gp per item function; and a living plant that has been magically altered.

spells.name: Azundel's Purification
spells.range: 3 yards / One item or volume of liquid or raw materials no greater than the caster's body volume / —
spells.effect: The more potent version of *Obar's lesser purification*. Destroys curses, magical tracers, and remnants of previous magics, and additionally expunges existing wizard spells and wizard-imposed spell-like abilities without triggering them. Priest spells and priest-imposed abilities on the item are not removed but glow to indicate their presence. Does not trigger, alter, or identify any dweomers. Also purges liquids of natural or magical impurities simultaneously. Does not affect recently living or undead materials. Cast twice on the same item (regardless of time between castings), all component parts of the item are refined to the finest possible state: internal and visible imperfections removed, craftsmanship raised to the highest level, making the item ready for the most powerful and complex enchantments. *Material components:* a pinch of dust from a powdered focal stone, a flawless diamond of any size or value, and at least three drops of a *potion of sweet water.*

spells.name: Blood Link
spells.effect: Can only be used in conjunction with a *permanency* or *permanency prayer* spell; must be cast within 1 turn of either to have any effect. Drains the 1-point Constitution loss involved in casting permanency from a touched sentient creature instead of from the caster. Unwitting or unwilling targets save to negate the loss. If the target can move and is hostile or suspicious, a successful attack roll is required to touch them. Good- and neutral-aligned casters risk alignment shift unless divine command or other mitigating circumstances apply. *Material components:* a short chain carved from zalantar wood, three walnut shell halves, and a drop of blood.

spells.name: Dweomer Divination
spells.effect: Reveals information about an enchanted item in a sequential unfolding process, one category of information per round, until the spell expires or all information has been gained. A repeat casting on a previously examined item skips already-known information. Sequence: (1) all dweomers present; (2) alignment/class restrictions and special benefits; (3) primary function fully revealed (how it works); (4) words of activation for the primary power; (5) any flaws or gaps in the primary power. This cycle repeats for each additional power in descending order of strength, then reveals control words and restrictions, recharging methods, and finally images of how the item was made. On normal (non-enchanted) items, performs as a sophisticated *detect magic* only. Ends immediately if the caster loses contact with the item for a full round or if the item has no dweomer. Provides no protection against curses or traps identified in the process, and may not reveal unintended side effects. Note: even non-enchanted items can bear trace dweomers if touched by spells — lasting 1 day per spell level for normal spells, and months or years per spell level for permanent or trigger-based magics.

spells.name: Dweomerflow
spells.range: 20 yards or touch / — / One person or one item
spells.effect: Functionally identical to the wizard version, with one significant addition unique to the priest version: a **holy water font or consecrated altar** can accept up to a dozen flowed spells as a repository. Any being of the faith who touches the altar and wills the magics forth may release them one per round thereafter, with silent mental control over targeting. Beings unfamiliar with the stored magics need 1 round of contact per stored spell to identify and control them; one random magic is revealed at a time to beings of the same faith (or via *dweomer divination*). Spells of 5th level or higher must be accompanied by an *abeyance* cast on the altar or vessel within 1 turn of being flowed in, or they erupt at a random time and random target. Altars commonly store offensive spells for lesser priests defending holy ground; damaging, defiling, or using cold iron on an altar almost always activates stored magics on the spot. ### 5th Level

spells.name: Abeyance
spells.range: Touch / — / 1 focal stone or 1 magical item
spells.effect: Identical in function to the wizard version. Freezes a spell held in a focal stone for indefinite suspension, or delays a magical item's next activation by 1 round.

spells.name: Eternal Flame
spells.school: 5 (Alteration, Necromancy) — Sphere: All, Elemental Fire, Necromantic
spells.range: Touch / One item or body not exceeding twice the caster's own body volume / —
spells.effect: Identical in function to the wizard version, with the same dual use on items and mammalian bodies. Imbues an item with a receptive neutral enchantment to hold magics; or fully attunes a body to receive the next spell at maximum potency with no saves or survival rolls required. Enchantment/charm and illusion/phantasm spells are exempt from the body-attuning effect in both versions. *Material component:* identical to the wizard version.

spells.name: Focal Stone
spells.range: Touch / — / 1 clear or translucent crystalline gemstone no larger than the caster's balled fist
spells.effect: Identical in function to the wizard version. Transforms the internal structure of a qualifying gemstone to hold a spell dweomer. Same glow, same poison-neutralization property, same immunity to heat and cold but not crushing. *Material component:* identical — a pinch of opal dust. ### 6th Level

spells.name: Higher Consecration
spells.effect: Dedicates an item to the service of the caster's deity, cleansing it of all other influences and other deities' marks. The item makes a saving throw using the caster's save vs. spell, modified cumulatively: +1 if crafted by or for the faith; +1 if cast on a consecrated altar or sacred ground; +1 if at the deity's express or dream command; +1 if all material components were personally made or gathered by the caster; –1 if unholy water is omitted; –1 if holy water is omitted; –2 if plain water is used; –2 if the item is known to be flawed or incomplete. Success is typically shown by a brief levitation and blue-white glow, though the deity may choose another color, wreathe the item in flame, or make it vanish if the priest is deemed unworthy. *Material components:* the priest's holy symbol; a spark struck from flint by cold iron (all three consumed in casting); a pinch of dung-heap earth on which plants have grown; a drop of holy water; a drop of unholy water; and a sealed vial of air from an enclosed space in which a dragon used its breath weapon within 1 turn of sealing.

spells.name: Holy Might
spells.range: Touch / One item no larger in volume than twice the caster's body volume / —
spells.effect: Priest counterpart to *Veladar's Vambrace*. Strengthens inorganic substances against rot and age. Same rule on organic content (must be less than one-tenth by volume). Purges fractures and blemishes; item appears like new. Grants +6 (vs. +5 for *Veladar's Vambrace*) on saving throws vs. acid, crushing blow, disintegration, fall, normal fire, and cold. Allows item volume up to twice the caster's body (vs. equal to the caster's body for the wizard version). *Material components:* a whole, unflawed ruby, emerald, or sapphire of not less than 3,000 gp value; a sliver or chunk of duskwood of the same size or larger; a piece of chitin of similar size from a beholder, ankheg, or bulette; a piece of obsidian of any size; and black dragon acid.

spells.name: Holy Vesting
spells.effect: Priest counterpart to *Wondrous Web*, with the same purpose and general mechanics: transfers magical powers from source items into a destination item at one power per round, creating a visible shimmering in the air between connected items. Key differences from *Wondrous Web*: the saving throws for drained items are higher (base 9 for fewer than three functions; base 11 plus one per function beyond four); and when cast on an altar dedicated to the caster's deity, the spell is immune to *dispel magic*. Missiles striking the caster during casting have the normal chance of ruining it, but after casting is complete only the caster's death or unconsciousness can end it prematurely. *Material components:* one drop of holy water consecrated to the caster's deity for the recipient item, plus one additional drop per source item; and a stick or block of burned incense. ### 7th Level

spells.name: Awakening
spells.effect: Identical in purpose to the wizard version. Key difference in the –1 modifier: co-contributors who are clergy of the same faith as the caster do **not** impose the penalty (wizard version penalizes all non-caster contributors). Additional bonus: +1 if the awakening is cast on or before an altar of the caster's deity. Otherwise identical saving throw modifiers and failure/success results. *Material components:* a priest spell scroll bearing at least as many spells as the item has functions; a gem of any kind worth at least 2,500 gp per function; and a living plant magically altered.

spells.name: Blood Link
spells.effect: Identical in function to the wizard version. *Material components:* a short chain carved from zalantar wood, a drop of blood, a drop of holy water, and a drop of unholy water (priest version adds holy and unholy water vs. the wizard version's three walnut shell halves).

spells.name: Dweomer Divination
spells.effect: Identical in function to the wizard version. Reveals enchantment details in the same sequential round-by-round structure: dweomers present, alignment/class restrictions, primary function, activation words, flaws/gaps — then repeating for secondary powers, then control words, recharging methods, and creation imagery.

spells.name: Permanency Prayer
spells.effect: Renders the enchantments on an item permanent. Cannot make the effects of cast spells permanent on a creature — only on an item's powers. Base 12-in-20 chance of success, modified cumulatively: +1 if cast on a consecrated altar or sacred spot; +1 if the caster performed an exceptional service for the deity within the season (and cast no other *permanency prayer* this season); +3 if the item is being made per the deity's direct or dream-vision command; –1 if the caster intends personal gain or aggrandizement; –2 if the item is flawed, damaged, or incomplete. Whether it succeeds or fails, the caster loses 1 point of Constitution (negated if a *blood link* has been cast within the previous turn to transfer the loss to another). The caster knows the outcome by a feeling of exaltation (success) or chill foreboding (failure) when touching the item after casting. No material components.

spells.name: Ritual of Transference
spells.effect: A cooperative ritual allowing participants to cast spells into a prepared item or being, transfer charges between items, or infuse an item or being with powers from another magical item, altar, or artifact. The caster must have physically touched the destination or at least one donor source at some prior time; no contact during casting is required. A continuous droning chant by at least one participant must be maintained throughout the casting turn; the original caster may stop chanting if others continue. Additional priests join by casting their own *ritual of transference* or a *combine* spell and touching the initial caster with bare flesh. After the casting turn, the ritual remains active for 1 turn during which participants cast spells or transfer charges into the recipient. Each incoming magic triggers a separate saving throw: for an item, base 12-in-20 per magic; for a being, normal save vs. spell. Cumulative modifiers: +2 per additional participating priest; +1 if the recipient is on or in an altar or sacred spot; –1 per magic contributed by a non-initial-caster; –1 per participant not serving the same deity; –2 if any hostile magic affects the recipient or any participant; –5 per participant slain or deliberately wounded during casting. Only spell-like powers can be transferred into beings; purely mechanical item abilities cannot. Beings can later release stored magics by act of will or absorb them as healing energy (one release per round). *Material components* (specific not stated in the text; implied to include prayer materials and holy implements). ## Metal Treatments (pp. 58–59) These are not spells but durable material processes that modify metal permanently. Blueshine has since been reproduced as a wizard spell; Everbright has not. ### Blueshine ### Everbright
